68:48: The words of God the Most High: "Indeed, those who dispute concerning Our verses..." Ibn Abbas said: Disbelief is putting words in the wrong places. Qatada and others said: It is disbelief and stubbornness. The words of God the Most High: "They are not hidden from Us" contain a severe threat and a firm warning, meaning that God the Most High knows who disputes concerning His verses, names, and attributes and will reward them for that with punishment and chastisement. For this reason God the Most High said: "Is one who is thrown into the Fire better or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?" Meaning, are these and that the same? They are not. Then the Almighty said as a threat to the disbelievers: Do whatever you will. Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and Ata’ Al-Khurasani said: Do whatever you will. This is a threat, whether good or evil. He knows you and is All-Seeing of your deeds. That is why He said: Indeed, He is All-Seeing of what you do. Then the Almighty said: Indeed, those who disbelieved in the message when it came to them. Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, and Qatadah said: And indeed, it is a mighty Book. That is, impregnable, and no one could come up with anything like it. Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it. That is, falsehood has no way to it because it was sent down by the Lord of the Worlds. That is why He said: A revelation from One Who is Wise, Praiseworthy. That is, Wise in His words and deeds. Praiseworthy in the sense of praiseworthy, that is, in all that He commands and forbids, all of its consequences and goals are praiseworthy. Then the Almighty said: Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. Qatada, As-Suddi and others said: “Nothing is said to you of denial except what was said to the messengers before you. So just as you lied, they lied, and just as they were patient with the harm that their people did to them, so be patient with the harm that your people do to you.” This is the preference of Ibn Jarir, and neither he nor Ibn Abi Hatim narrated anything else. The Almighty’s statement: Indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness means for those who repent to Him. And the Possessor of painful punishment means for those who persist in their disbelief, transgression, stubbornness, dissension and opposition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa ibn Ismail told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab, who said: This verse was revealed: Indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Were it not for the forgiveness and pardon of God, no one would enjoy life, and were it not for His threat and punishment, everyone would be tired. God Almighty says: So be patient O Muhammad, with your people's harm to you and their denial, for God will judge you against them and make the outcome for you and your followers in this world and the hereafter. And do not be like the companion of the fish meaning Dhul-Nun, who is Jonah, son of Matta, peace be upon him, when he went angry with his people. What happened to him was that he rode into the sea and the fish swallowed him and the fish wandered with him in the seas and the darkness of the deep sea, and he heard the sea and what was in it glorifying the Most High, the Almighty, who does not reject what He has implemented of decree. Then he called out in the darkness, "There is no god except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers." God Almighty said: "So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers." God Almighty said: And had he not been among those who glorify God, he would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected. And He said here: When he called out while he was distressed. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and As-Suddi said: And he was distressed. Ata' said: Al-Khurasani and Abu Malik: He was distressed. We have already mentioned in the hadith that when he said: “There is no god but You, glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers,” the word came out encircling the throne. The angels said: O Lord, this is a weak, well-known voice from a strange land. God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: Do you not know this? They said: No. He said: This is Yunus. They said: O Lord, Your servant, whose righteous deeds and answered supplications are continually being raised up to Him? He said: Yes. They said: Will You not have mercy on what he did in times of ease and save him from calamity? So God commanded the whale to throw him out onto the shore. For this reason, God, the Most High, said: So his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous. Imam Ahmad said: “Waki’ narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘It is not appropriate for anyone to say, “I am better than Jonah, son of Matta.”’ Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, and it is in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. God, the Most High, said: Those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others said: They would almost make you slip means they would pierce you with their eyes, meaning they would envy you with their eyes, because of their hatred for you, were it not for God’s protection and safeguarding you from them. This verse is evidence that the evil eye’s affliction and effect are real by the command of God, the Almighty, as has been reported in the hadiths narrated through many different chains of narration. Hadith of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him Abu Dawud said: Sulayman bin Dawud al-Atki told us, Sharik told us H and al-Abbas al-Anbari told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Sharik told us on the authority of al-Abbas bin Dharih on the authority of al-Sha’bi, al-Abbas said on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye, a fever, or blood that cannot be stopped. Al-Abbas did not mention the evil eye, and this is the wording of Sulayman. The hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husaib (may God be pleased with him Abu Abdullah ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr told us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Razi, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Buraydah ibn al-Husaib, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a fever. This is how Ibn Majah narrated it. Muslim included it in his Sahih on the authority of Sa`id ibn Mansur, on the authority of Hishayn ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of `Amir al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Buraydah, with a missing chain of transmission, and there is a story in it. Shu`bah narrated it on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Buraydah. This hadith was narrated by al-Bukhari on the authority of Muhammad ibn Fadil, Abu Dawud on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, and al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah, all three of them on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of `Amir al-Sha`bi, on the authority of `Imran ibn Husayn, with a missing chain of transmission: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a fever. Hadith of Abu Dharr Jundub bin Junada, may God be pleased with him Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Arara bin Al-Yazid Al-Sami told us, Daylam bin Ghazwan told us, Wahb bin Abi Dani told us, on the authority of Abu Harb, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The evil eye afflicts a man, by God’s permission, and he soars high, then falls from it. Its chain of transmission is strange, and they did not include it. Hadith of Habis At-Tamimi Imam Ahmad said: Abd Al-Samad told us, Harb told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us, Hayyah bin Habis At-Tamimi told me that his father told him that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: There is nothing wrong with a squint, and the evil eye is true, and the most truthful omen is an omen. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Ali, on the authority of Abu Ghassan Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ali bin Mubarak, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, with it, then he said: It is strange. And he said: Sinan narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Hayyah bin Habis, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I say: Imam Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Hasan bin Musa and Husayn bin Muhammad, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Hayyah, who told him on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There is nothing wrong with a squint, and the evil eye is true, and the most truthful omen is an omen. Hadith of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Duraid, Ismail bin Thauban told me, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The evil eye is real, the evil eye is real and brings down the witch. Strange. Another chain of transmission Muslim said in his Sahih: Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Darimi told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Wahib told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The evil eye is real, and if anything could overtake destiny, it would be the evil eye. And when you are asked to wash, then wash.” He is the only one who transmitted it, not Al-Bukhari. Abdul Razzaq said, on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Minhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, used to seek refuge for Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, saying: I seek refuge for you in the perfect words of God from every devil and pest, and from every evil eye. And he would say: This is how Ibrahim used to seek refuge for Isaac and Ishmael, peace be upon them. Al-Bukhari and the Sunan scholars transmitted it from the hadith of Al-Minhal with it. Hadith of Abu Umamah As`ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, may God be pleased with him Ibn Majah said: Hisham ibn `Ammar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Umamah As`ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: “`Amir ibn Rabi`ah passed by Sahl ibn Hunayf while he was bathing and said: I have never seen anything like today, nor such hideous skin. It was not long before he was struck by a snake, and he was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said to him: ‘He caught Sahl lying dead.’ He said: ‘Who do you accuse?’ They said: ‘`Amir ibn Rabi`ah.’ He said: ‘Why would one of you kill his brother? If one of you sees something he likes in his brother, let him pray for blessings for him.’ Then he called for water and ordered `Amir to perform ablution, washing his face and hands up to the elbows, his knees, and the inside of his lower garment, and he ordered him to pour water over himself.” Sufyan said: Mu`mar said, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, and he ordered that the vessel be tipped over from behind him. Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah and Malik ibn Anas, both of them from Al-Zuhri with it, and from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah also narrated it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Umamah: The vessel should be tipped over from behind. And from the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi’b on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Umamah: As’ad ibn Sahl ibn Hanif on the authority of his father on his authority. And from the hadith of Malik also on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl on the authority of his father on his authority. Hadith of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Sa`id bin Sulayman told us, `Ibad told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek protection from the eyes of the jinn and the eyes of mankind. When the two Mu`awwidhat were revealed, he took them and left everything else. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Sa`id bin Iyas Abu Mas`ud Al-Jariry, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan. Another hadith from him Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, my father told me, Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhaib told me, Abu Nadrah told me, on the authority of Abu Sa`id, “That Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Are you ill, O Muhammad? He said: Yes. He said: In the name of God I perform ruqyah over you from everything that is harming you, and from the evil of every soul and eye that is harming you, and God heals you. In the name of God I perform ruqyah over you.” And he narrated it on the authority of Affan on the authority of Abd al-Warith, similarly. Muslim and the people of Sunan, except Abu Dawud, narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Warith with it. Imam Ahmad also said: Affan told us, Wahib told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed or Jabir ibn Abdullah, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell ill, so Gabriel came to him and said, ‘In the name of God, I perform ruqyah over you from everything that is harming you, from every envier and evil eye, and God will heal you.’” It was also narrated by Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Tafawi, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on its authority. Abu Zur’ah al-Razi said: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Abu Nadra, and on the authority of Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Anas, with a similar meaning, and both are authentic. Hadith of Abu Hurairah (may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Ma'mar told us, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurairah told us, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: The evil eye is real. Both of them narrated it from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq. Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah, on the authority of al-Jariry, on the authority of Mudharib ibn Hazn, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The evil eye is real. He was the only one who narrated it. Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah, on the authority of Saeed al-Jariry, and Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numair told us, Thawr - meaning Ibn Yazid - told us, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The evil eye is real, and Satan and the envy of the sons of Adam attend to it. Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid told us, Abu Ma'shar told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays: Abu Hurairah was asked: Did you hear the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: “Superstition is in three things: in a dwelling, a horse, and a woman?” He said: I said, then, should I say about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something he did not say, but I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, The most truthful omen is the omen, and the evil eye is true. The hadith of Asma bint Umays Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Urwah ibn Amir, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Rifa’ah az-Zurqi, who said: “Asma said, ‘O Messenger of God, the children of Ja’far are afflicted by the evil eye. Should I recite ruqyah for them?’ He said, ‘Yes, for if anything could overtake destiny, it would be the evil eye.’” This is how it was narrated by at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah with this chain of transmission. It was also narrated by at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa’i from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Urwah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Urwah ibn Amir, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Rifa’ah, on the authority of Asma bint Umays with this chain of transmission. At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan saheeh. Hadith of Aisha (may God be pleased with her Ibn Majah said: Ali ibn Abi Al-Khasib told us, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan and Mis’ar, on the authority of Ma’bad ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded her to seek protection from the evil eye. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Kathir, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ma’bad ibn Khalid, and Muslim included it on the authority of Sufyan and Mis’ar, both on the authority of Ma’bad, on his authority. Then Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abu Hisham Al-Makhzumi told us, Wahib told us, on the authority of Abu Waqid, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Seek refuge in God, for the evil eye is real. He is the only one who narrated it. Abu Dawud said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The one who cast the evil eye would be ordered to perform ablution and wash the one who had been affected by it. I said likewise that Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Hasan bin Musa and Husayn bin Muhammad on the authority of Sinan that Ibn Hasana told him on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no inspiration, and the evil eye is real, and the most truthful omen is the omens. Hadith of Sahl ibn Hanif Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us. Abu Uwais told us. Al-Zuhri narrated to us on the authority of Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, that his father told him: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and they walked with him towards Mecca until they reached the ravine of Al-Kharrar in Al-Juhfah. Sahl ibn Hunayf washed himself. He was a white man with a handsome body and skin. Amir ibn Rabi’ah, the brother of Banu ‘Adi ibn Ka’b, looked at him while he was washing and said: ‘I have never seen anything like today, nor skin as hidden.’ Sahl became weak and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was approached and it was said to him: ‘O Messenger of God, what do you think of Sahl? By God, he does not raise his head nor does he recover.’ He said: ‘Do you accuse anyone of him?’ They said: ‘Amir ibn Rabi’ah looked at him.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Amir and became angry with him and said: ‘Why would one of you kill his brother? Why don’t you, when you see something that pleases you, bless him?’ Then he said: ‘Gaze for him.’ He washed his face, hands, elbows, knees, the tips of his feet, and the inside of his lower garment in a cup. Then he poured that water over him. A man poured it over his head and back from behind him, then he poured it over his head and back from behind him. The cup was behind him, so he did that and Sahl went with the people without any problem.” Hadith of Amir bin Rabi’ah Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: We were told by Wakee’, we were told by my father, we were told by Abdullah bin Isa, on the authority of Umayyah bin Hind bin Sahl bin Hunaif, on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Amir, who said: Amir bin Rabi’ah and Sahl bin Hunaif set out intending to perform ablution. He said: They set out looking for wine. He said: Amir put down the woolen cloak he was wearing, and I looked at him and caught his eye. He went down into the water to bathe. He said: I heard a crackling sound in the water, so I went to him and called out to him three times, but he did not answer me. So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He said: He came walking and waded into the water, and it was as if I could see the whiteness of his shins. He said: He struck his chest with his hand and then said: O God, turn away from him its heat and its cold and its rain. He said: He stood up, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you sees something he likes in his brother, in himself, or in his wealth, then let him ask for blessings, for the evil eye is real. Hadith of Jabir Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Muhammad bin Muammar narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Talib bin Habib bin Amr bin Sahl Al-Ansari, who is called Ibn Al-Dajji’, the companion of Hamza, may God be pleased with him, narrated to me Abdul Rahman bin Jabir bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘Most of those who die from my nation after the Book of God, His judgment and decree are because of the souls.’” Al-Bazzar said: He meant the evil eye. He said: We do not know of this hadith being narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, except with this chain of transmission. I said: Rather, it has been narrated from Jabir through another chain of transmission. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdul Rahman Muhammad bin Al-Mundhir Al-Harawi, known as Shukr, said in his book Al-Aja’ib, which contains important and strange benefits: Al-Ramadi narrated to us, Ya’qub bin Muhammad narrated to us, Ali bin Abi Ali Al-Hashemi narrated to us, Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir narrated to us, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘The evil eye is real, for it leads a man to the grave and a camel to the cooking pot. Most of the destruction of my nation is because of the evil eye.’” Then he narrated it on the authority of Shu`ayb ibn Ayoub, on the authority of Mu`awiyah ibn Hisham, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A man may enter the grave with an eye, and a camel may enter the cooking pot. This chain of transmission is all trustworthy, but it was not included in the Sahih. Hadith of Abdullah bin Amr Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah told us, Rashdin bin Saad told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Thauban, on the authority of Hisham bin Abi Ruqayyah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no contagion, no bad omen, no evil eye, no envy, and the evil eye is real. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Hadith on the authority of Ali Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Khaithama bin Sulaiman Al-Hafiz, who said: Ubaid bin Muhammad Al-Kashuri told us, Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Abd Rabbih Al-Basri told us on the authority of Abu Raja’ on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, “That Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and found him sad, so he said: O Muhammad, what is this sadness that I see on your face? He said: Al-Hasan and Al-Hussain have been afflicted by the evil eye. He said: He spoke the truth about the evil eye, for the evil eye is real, so why don’t you protect them with these words? He said: What are they, O Gabriel?” He said: Say: O God, Possessor of the mighty power and the ancient favor, Possessor of the noble face, Possessor of the perfect words and the answered supplications, save al-Hasan and al-Husayn from the souls of the jinn and the eyes of mankind. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said it, and they stood playing in front of him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Protect yourselves, your women, and your children with this incantation, for no one has ever sought protection with anything like it. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said: Abu Raja Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hanti from the people of Tustar was the only one who narrated it. Ibn Asakir mentioned him in the biography of Tarad ibn al-Husayn in his history. And the Almighty said: {And they say: He is mad} meaning they look down on him with their eyes and hurt him with their tongues and they say: He is mad, meaning because he came with the Qur’an. God the Almighty said: {And it is not but a reminder to the worlds} [the end of the interpretation of Surah Nun]. And to God be praise and thanks.
68:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Qalam In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful We have already discussed the letters of the alphabet at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, and that the Almighty’s saying Nun is like His saying Sad, “Qaf,” and similar disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs. The explanation of that is clearer than repeating it here. It was said that what is meant by the saying Nun is a great whale on the great, surrounding current of water, and it carries the seven earths, as Imam Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan - he is Al-Thawri - told us, Sulayman - he is Al-A’mash - told us, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing that God created was the pen. He said: Write. He said: What should I write? He said: Write down the destiny. So he wrote down what would happen from that day until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the Noon and raised the water vapor, from which the heavens burst forth and the earth was spread out on the back of the Noon. The Noon shook and the earth shook and was fixed with mountains, so they stand tall on the earth. And thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Sinan on the authority of Abu Muawiyah on the authority of Al-A’mash on his authority. And thus Shu’bah, Muhammad ibn Fadil, and Waki’ narrated it on the authority of Al-A’mash on his authority. And Shu`bah added in his narration, then he recited, “Nun. By the pen and what they write.” Sharik narrated it on the authority of Al-A`mash on the authority of Abu Dhibyan or Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so he mentioned something similar to it. Mu`mar narrated it on the authority of Al-A`mash that Ibn Abbas said: So he mentioned it, then he recited, “Nun. By the pen and what they write.” Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, created was the pen, then He said to it: Write, so it wrote what will be until the Hour comes, then He created the nun above the water, then He pressed the earth down upon it. Al-Tabarani narrated this with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: Abu Habib Zaid bin Al-Mahdi Al-Marwazi told us, Saeed bin Yaqub Al-Talaqani told us, Muammil bin Ismail told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha Muslim bin Subaih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first thing God created was the Pen and the Whale. Then He said to al-Qalam 68:Write. It said: What should I write? He said: Everything will be until the Day of Resurrection.” Then he recited: “Nun. By the Pen and what they inscribe.” So the Nun is the Whale, and the Pen is the Pen. Another hadith on this was narrated by Ibn Asakir on the authority of Abu Abdullah, the client of the Umayyads, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first thing God created was the pen. Then He created the nun, which is the inkwell. Then He said to it: Write. It said: What should I write? He said: Write what will be - or what will be - of deeds, provision, effect, or lifespan. So He wrote that until the Day of Resurrection. This is His saying: ‘Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.’ Then He sealed the pen, so it did not speak until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the intellect and said: By My glory, I will perfect you among those I love and diminish you among those I hate.” Ibn Abi Nujayh said: Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr told him on the authority of Mujahid who said: It was said that the Nun is the great whale that is under the seventh earth. Al-Baghawi and a group of commentators mentioned that on the back of this whale is a rock as thick as the heavens and the earth, and on its back is a bull with forty thousand horns, and on its back are the seven earths and what is in them and what is between them, and God knows best. It is strange that some of them interpreted this meaning of the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Ismail told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas that Abdullah bin Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, so he came to him and asked him about some things. He said, I am going to ask you about things that only a prophet knows. He said, What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food that the people of Paradise will eat? Why does the child gravitate toward his father? Why does the child gravitate toward his mother? He said, Gabriel told me about them just now. Ibn Salam said, That is the enemy of the Jews from the angels. He said, “As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather them from the east to the west, and the first food that the people of Paradise will eat is the extra liver of a fish. As for the child, if the man’s semen precedes the woman’s semen, the child will be born, and if the woman’s semen precedes the man’s semen, the woman will be born.” Al-Bukhari narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Hamid, and Muslim also narrated it. He has a hadith from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to this. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Asma’ al-Rahbi, on the authority of Thawban, “A rabbi asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, On issues, one of which was that he said: “What is their gift?” meaning the people of Paradise when they enter Paradise? He said: The extra liver of a whale. He said: What is their food after that? He said: The bull of Paradise that used to eat from its edges will be slaughtered for them. He said: What is their drink after that? He said: From a spring in it called Salsabil. It was said that what is meant by his saying: N is a tablet of light. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan bin Shabib Al-Maktab narrated to us, Muhammad bin Ziyad Al-Jazari narrated to us, on the authority of Furat bin Abi Al-Furat, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurrah, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Nun. By the Pen and what they write.’ A tablet of light and a pen of light that records what will be until the Day of Resurrection.” This is a strange mursal narration. Ibn Jurayj said: I was told that that pen of light is one hundred years long. It was said that what is meant by his saying Nun is an inkwell, and the pen is the pen. Ibn Jarir said: Abd Al-A’la narrated to us, Abu Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Qatadah, regarding his saying Nun, they said that it is the inkwell. A very strange hadith has been narrated in this regard, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham bin Khalid narrated to us, Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, Abu Abdullah, the client of the Umayyads, narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God created the nun, and it is the inkwell. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yaqub told us, my brother Isa bin Abdullah told us, Thabit Ath-Thamali told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God created the inkwell, and created the pen, and said: Write. He said: What should I write? He said: Write everything that will occur until the Day of Resurrection of deeds done righteous or wicked, or allocated provision, lawful or unlawful. Then He made everything of that obligatory in its nature, its entry into this world, its duration in it, and its exit from it. Then He appointed guardians over the servants and keepers of the Book. The guardians copy from the guardians every day the deeds of that day. Then when the provision is exhausted, the record is cut off, and the appointed time has passed, the guardians come to the keepers asking for the deeds of that day. The guardians say to them: We do not find anything for your companion with us. Then the guardians return and find that they have died. Ibn Abbas said: Are you not an Arab people who hear the guardians say: We used to copy what you used to do. And can copying be anything other than from an original? God the Almighty said: And the pen apparently refers to the same type of pen that is used to write, as in His statement: Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous * Who taught by the pen * Taught man that which he knew not. So it is an oath from Him the Almighty and a reminder to His creation of the blessing He bestowed upon them of learning to write by which knowledge is attained. For this reason He said: and what they inscribe Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: It means what they write. Abu Ad-Dhaha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: and what they inscribe means what they do. As-Suddi said: and what they inscribe means the angels and what they write of the deeds of the servants. Others said: Rather, what is meant here is the pen that God made move by decree when He wrote down the destinies of creation, fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. They mentioned in this regard the hadiths that mention the pen. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed bin Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan and Yunus bin Habib told us: Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi told us, Abdul Wahid bin Salim Al-Sulami told us, on the authority of Ata’, who is Ibn Abi Rabah, Al-Walid bin Ubadah bin Al-Samit told me: My father called me when death was approaching him and said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it, ‘Write.’ It said, ‘O Lord, what should I write?’ It said, ‘Write the destiny and what will be forever.’” This hadith was narrated by Imam Ahmad through various chains of narration on the authority of Al-Walid bin Ubadah on the authority of his father on this authority. Al-Tirmidhi included it on the authority of Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi on this authority, and he said, It is hasan saheeh ghareeb. It was narrated by Abu Dawud in his book, As-Sunnah, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Musafir, on the authority of Yahya ibn Hassan, on the authority of Ibn Rabah, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubla, on the authority of Abu Hafsah, whose name was Habish ibn Shuraih Al-Habashi Ash-Shami, on the authority of Ubadah, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah At-Tusi told us, Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq told us, Abdullah ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Rabah ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Habib, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to narrate that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The first thing that God created was the pen, and He commanded it to write everything. This is strange from this chain of narration, and they did not include it. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: The pen means that with which the remembrance is written. And the statement of God, and what they inscribe means what they write, as mentioned above. His statement: You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman means, praise be to God, you are not a madman as the ignorant among your people say, who deny the guidance and clear truth that you have brought them, and they attribute madness to you because of it. And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted means, rather, for you is a great reward and a bountiful recompense that does not cease or perish for conveying the message of your Lord to creation and your patience in the face of their harm. The meaning of uninterrupted is not cut off like His statement, a gift that is not cut off, so for them is a reward uninterrupted meaning, it is not cut off from them. Mujahid said: uninterrupted means not counted, and this goes back to what we have said. God the Almighty says: {And indeed, you are of a great moral character}. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: {And indeed, you are of a great religion, which is Islam}. Mujahid, Abu Malik, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said the same, as did Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd. Atiyyah said: {And indeed, you are of great manners}. Muammar said on the authority of Qatadah: Aisha was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {His character was the Qur’an}. She said as it is in the Qur’an. Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba said on the authority of Qatadah regarding His statement: {And indeed, you are of a great moral character}. It was mentioned to us that Sa’d ibn Hisham asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {Do you not recite the Qur’an?} He said: {Yes}. She said: {The character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the Qur’an}. Abdur-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Zurara ibn Awfa on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham who said: I asked Aisha and said: {Tell me, O Mother of the Believers, about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {Do you recite the Qur’an?} I said: {Yes}. She said: {His character was the Qur’an}. This is an abbreviation of a long hadith. Imam Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Qatada in full, and it will come in Surat Al-Muzzammil, God willing, and he is trustworthy. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and she said: His character was the Qur’an. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Wahb, on the authority of a man from Banu Sawad, who said: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and she said: Do you not recite the Qur’an? And indeed, you are of a great moral character. He said: I said: Tell me about that. She said: I made him food and Hafsah made him food, and I said to my slave girl, Go, and if she brings the food and sets it down before me, throw the food away. She said: So she brought the food, and the slave girl threw it, and the bowl fell and broke, and it was a cutlery. She said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) gathered it and said: Retrieve - or Aswad was unsure - Retrieve - a container in place of your container. She said: So he did not say anything. Ibn Jarir said: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Al-Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham, who said: I came to Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, and said to her: Tell me about the character of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: His character was the Qur’an. Do you not read: And indeed, you are of a great moral character? Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated something similar from the hadith of Al-Hasan. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Mu’awiyah ibn Salih informed me, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahriyyah, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: I performed Hajj and went to Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and asked her about the character of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: The character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Qur’an. Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, and An-Nasa’i narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Ishaq ibn Mansur, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Salih, with this same chain of transmission. This means that, peace and blessings be upon him, obeying the Quran’s commands and prohibitions became his nature, a characteristic that was inherent in him, and he abandoned his innate nature. Whatever the Quran commanded him to do, he did, and whatever it forbade him from doing, he abandoned. This was in addition to the great character traits that God created in him, such as modesty, generosity, courage, forgiveness, and patience, and every beautiful character trait, as proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Anas, who said: I served the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, for ten years, and he never once said to me uff, nor did he say about something I did, Why did you do that? nor about something I did not do, Why didn’t you do that? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the best of people in character. I have never touched silk or brocade or anything softer than the hand of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), nor have I smelled musk or perfume that was more fragrant than the sweat of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq bin Mansur told us, Ibrahim bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Al-Bara’ say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) had the most handsome face and the best character. He was neither tall nor short. There are many hadiths on this. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi has a book on this in his book Al-Shama’il. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never struck a servant of his with his hand, nor did he strike a woman, nor did he strike anything with his hand except when he was fighting in the cause of God. He never gave a choice between two things except that the lesser of the two was more beloved to him, until it was a sin. But if it was a sin, he was the furthest of people from sin. He never took revenge for himself from something that was done to him, except when the sacred limits of God were violated, in which case he would take revenge for the sake of God, the Almighty and Majestic. Imam Ahmad said: Saeed ibn Mansur told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, on the authority of al-Qa’qa’ ibn Hakim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was only sent to perfect good character. He is the only one who transmitted it. And the saying of God the Almighty: Then you will see, and they will see * Which of you is the one who is afflicted. So you will know, O Muhammad, and your opponents and those who deny you will know who is the one who is afflicted and misguided among you and among them. This is like His saying the Almighty: They will know tomorrow who is the most evil liar. And His saying the Almighty: And either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said about this verse, You will know, and they will know on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Which of you is afflicted means the insane. Mujahid and others said the same. Qatadah and others said: Which of you is afflicted means the most deserving of Satan. The meaning of the one who is afflicted is clear: the one who has been afflicted and has gone astray from the truth. The preposition with was added to His saying which of you to indicate the inclusion of the verb in His saying Then you will see, and they will see. The meaning is: You will know, and they will know, or You will inform, and they will inform, which of you is the one who is afflicted. And God knows best. Then God Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided. That is, He, the Almighty, knows which of the two groups among you is the one who is guided, and He knows which party has strayed from the truth.

The explanation of that is clearer than repeating it here. It was said: What is meant by the saying Nun is a great whale on the great, surrounding current of water, and it carries the seven earths, as Imam Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan - he is Al-Thawri - told us, Sulayman - he is Al-A’mash - told us, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing that God created was the pen. He said: Write. He said: What should I write? He said: Write down the destiny. So he wrote down what would happen from that day until the Day of Resurrection. The Noon shook and the earth shook and was fixed with mountains, so they stand tall on the earth. And thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Sinan on the authority of Abu Muawiyah on the authority of Al-A’mash on his authority. And thus Shu’bah, Muhammad ibn Fadil, and Waki’ narrated it on the authority of Al-A’mash on his authority. And Shu`bah added in his narration, then he recited, “Nun. She said: {His character was the Qur’an}. She said as it is in the Qur’an. Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba said on the authority of Qatadah regarding His statement: {And indeed, you are of a great moral character}. It was mentioned to us that Sa’d ibn Hisham asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {Do you not recite the Qur’an?} He said: {Yes}. She said: {The character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the Qur’an}. Abdur-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Zurara ibn Awfa on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham who said: I asked Aisha and said: {Tell me, O Mother of the Believers, about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {Do you recite the Qur’an?} I said: {Yes}. She said: {His character was the Qur’an}. This is an abbreviation of a long hadith. Imam Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Qatada in full, and it will come in Surat Al-Muzzammil, God willing, and he is trustworthy. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and she said: His character was the Qur’an. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Wahb, on the authority of a man from Banu Sawad, who said: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and she said: Do you not recite the Qur’an? And indeed, you are of a great moral character. He said: I said: Tell me about that. She said: I made him food and Hafsah made him food, and I said to my slave girl, Go, and if she brings the food and sets it down before me, throw the food away. She said: So she brought the food, and the slave girl threw it, and the bowl fell and broke, and it was a cutlery. She said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) gathered it and said: Retrieve - or Aswad was unsure - Retrieve - a container in place of your container. She said: So he did not say anything. Ibn Jarir said: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Al-Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham, who said: I came to Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, and said to her: Tell me about the character of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: His character was the Qur’an. Do you not read: And indeed, you are of a great moral character? Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated something similar from the hadith of Al-Hasan. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Mu’awiyah ibn Salih informed me, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahriyyah, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: I performed Hajj and went to Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and asked her about the character of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: The character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Qur’an. Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, and An-Nasa’i narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Ishaq ibn Mansur, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Salih, with this same chain of transmission. This means that, peace and blessings be upon him, obeying the Quran’s commands and prohibitions became his nature, a characteristic that was inherent in him, and he abandoned his innate nature. Whatever the Quran commanded him to do, he did, and whatever it forbade him from doing, he abandoned. This was in addition to the great character traits that God created in him, such as modesty, generosity, courage, forgiveness, and patience, and every beautiful character trait, as proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Anas, who said: I served the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, for ten years, and he never once said to me uff, nor did he say about something I did, Why did you do that? nor about something I did not do, Why didn’t you do that? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the best of people in character. I have never touched silk or brocade or anything softer than the hand of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), nor have I smelled musk or perfume that was more fragrant than the sweat of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq bin Mansur told us, Ibrahim bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Al-Bara’ say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) had the most handsome face and the best character. He was neither tall nor short. There are many hadiths on this. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi has a book on this in his book Al-Shama’il. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never struck a servant of his with his hand, nor did he strike a woman, nor did he strike anything with his hand except when he was fighting in the cause of God. He never gave a choice between two things except that the lesser of the two was more beloved to him, until it was a sin. But if it was a sin, he was the furthest of people from sin. He never took revenge for himself from something that was done to him, except when the sacred limits of God were violated, in which case he would take revenge for the sake of God, the Almighty and Majestic. Imam Ahmad said: Saeed ibn Mansur told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, on the authority of al-Qa’qa’ ibn Hakim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was only sent to perfect good character. He is the only one who transmitted it. And the saying of God the Almighty: Then you will see, and they will see * Which of you is the one who is afflicted. So you will know, O Muhammad, and your opponents and those who deny you will know who is the one who is afflicted and misguided among you and among them. This is like His saying the Almighty: They will know tomorrow who is the most evil liar. And His saying the Almighty: And either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error. Mujahid and others said the same. Qatadah and others said: Which of you is afflicted means the most deserving of Satan. The meaning of the one who is afflicted is clear: the one who has been afflicted and has gone astray from the truth. The preposition with was added to His saying which of you to indicate the inclusion of the verb in His saying Then you will see, and they will see. The meaning is: You will know, and they will know, or You will inform, and they will inform, which of you is the one who is afflicted. And God knows best. Then God Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided. That is, He, the Almighty, knows which of the two groups among you is the one who is guided, and He knows which party has strayed from the truth.
68:3: We have already discussed the letters of the alphabet at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, and that the Almighty’s saying: Nun is like His saying Sad, “Qaf,” and similar disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs. The explanation of that is clearer than repeating it here. It was said: What is meant by the saying Nun is a great whale on the great, surrounding current of water, and it carries the seven earths, as Imam Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan - he is Al-Thawri - told us, Sulayman - he is Al-A’mash - told us, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing that God created was the pen. He said: Write. He said: What should I write? He said: Write down the destiny. So he wrote down what would happen from that day until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the Noon and raised the water vapor, from which the heavens burst forth and the earth was spread out on the back of the Noon. The Noon shook and the earth shook and was fixed with mountains, so they stand tall on the earth. And thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Sinan on the authority of Abu Muawiyah on the authority of Al-A’mash on his authority. And thus Shu’bah, Muhammad ibn Fadil, and Waki’ narrated it on the authority of Al-A’mash on his authority. And Shu`bah added in his narration, then he recited, “Nun. By the pen and what they write.” Sharik narrated it on the authority of Al-A`mash on the authority of Abu Dhibyan or Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so he mentioned something similar to it. Mu`mar narrated it on the authority of Al-A`mash that Ibn Abbas said: So he mentioned it, then he recited, “Nun. By the pen and what they write.” Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, created was the pen, then He said to it: Write, so it wrote what will be until the Hour comes, then He created the nun above the water, then He pressed the earth down upon it. Al-Tabarani narrated this with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: Abu Habib Zaid bin Al-Mahdi Al-Marwazi told us, Saeed bin Yaqub Al-Talaqani told us, Muammil bin Ismail told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha Muslim bin Subaih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first thing God created was the Pen and the Whale. Then He said to al-Qalam 68:Write. It said: What should I write? He said: Everything will be until the Day of Resurrection.” Then he recited: “Nun. By the Pen and what they inscribe.” So the Nun is the Whale, and the Pen is the Pen. Another hadith on this was narrated by Ibn Asakir on the authority of Abu Abdullah, the client of the Umayyads, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first thing God created was the pen. Then He created the nun, which is the inkwell. Then He said to it: Write. It said: What should I write? He said: Write what will be - or what will be - of deeds, provision, effect, or lifespan. So He wrote that until the Day of Resurrection. This is His saying: ‘Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.’ Then He sealed the pen, so it did not speak until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the intellect and said: By My glory, I will perfect you among those I love and diminish you among those I hate.” Ibn Abi Nujayh said: Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr told him on the authority of Mujahid who said: It was said that the Nun is the great whale that is under the seventh earth. Al-Baghawi and a group of commentators mentioned that on the back of this whale is a rock as thick as the heavens and the earth, and on its back is a bull with forty thousand horns, and on its back are the seven earths and what is in them and what is between them, and God knows best. It is strange that some of them interpreted this meaning of the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Ismail told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas that Abdullah bin Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, so he came to him and asked him about some things. He said, I am going to ask you about things that only a prophet knows. He said, What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food that the people of Paradise will eat? Why does the child gravitate toward his father? Why does the child gravitate toward his mother? He said, Gabriel told me about them just now. Ibn Salam said, That is the enemy of the Jews from the angels. He said, “As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather them from the east to the west, and the first food that the people of Paradise will eat is the extra liver of a fish. As for the child, if the man’s semen precedes the woman’s semen, the child will be born, and if the woman’s semen precedes the man’s semen, the woman will be born.” Al-Bukhari narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Hamid, and Muslim also narrated it. He has a hadith from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to this. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Asma’ al-Rahbi, on the authority of Thawban, “A rabbi asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, On issues, one of which was that he said: “What is their gift?” meaning the people of Paradise when they enter Paradise? He said: The extra liver of a whale. He said: What is their food after that? He said: The bull of Paradise that used to eat from its edges will be slaughtered for them. He said: What is their drink after that? He said: From a spring in it called Salsabil. It was said that what is meant by his saying: N is a tablet of light. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan bin Shabib Al-Maktab narrated to us, Muhammad bin Ziyad Al-Jazari narrated to us, on the authority of Furat bin Abi Al-Furat, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurrah, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Nun. Ibn Jurayj said: I was told that that pen of light is one hundred years long. It was said that what is meant by his saying Nun is an inkwell, and the pen is the pen. Ibn Jarir said: Abd Al-A’la narrated to us, Abu Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Qatadah, regarding his saying Nun, they said that it is the inkwell. The guardians say to them: We do not find anything for your companion with us. Then the guardians return and find that they have died. Ibn Abbas said: Are you not an Arab people who hear the guardians say: We used to copy what you used to do. And can copying be anything other than from an original? God the Almighty said: "And the pen" apparently refers to the same type of pen that is used to write, as in His statement: "Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous * Who taught by the pen * Taught man that which he knew not." As-Suddi said: "and what they inscribe" means the angels and what they write of the deeds of the servants. They mentioned in this regard the hadiths that mention the pen. And the statement of God, and what they inscribe means what they write, as mentioned above.
