By the pen and what they write.” Sharik narrated it on the authority of Al-A`mash on the authority of Abu Dhibyan or Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so he mentioned something similar to it. Mu`mar narrated it on the authority of Al-A`mash that Ibn Abbas said: So he mentioned it, then he recited, “Nun. By the pen and what they write.” Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, created was the pen, then He said to it: Write, so it wrote what will be until the Hour comes, then He created the nun above the water, then He pressed the earth down upon it. Al-Tabarani narrated this with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: Abu Habib Zaid bin Al-Mahdi Al-Marwazi told us, Saeed bin Yaqub Al-Talaqani told us, Muammil bin Ismail told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha Muslim bin Subaih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first thing God created was the Pen and the Whale. Then He said to al-Qalam 68:Write. It said: What should I write? He said: Everything will be until the Day of Resurrection.” Then he recited: “Nun. By the Pen and what they inscribe.” So the Nun is the Whale, and the Pen is the Pen. Another hadith on this was narrated by Ibn Asakir on the authority of Abu Abdullah, the client of the Umayyads, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first thing God created was the pen. Then He created the nun, which is the inkwell. Then He said to it: Write. It said: What should I write? He said: Write what will be - or what will be - of deeds, provision, effect, or lifespan. So He wrote that until the Day of Resurrection. This is His saying: ‘Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.’ Then He sealed the pen, so it did not speak until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the intellect and said: By My glory, I will perfect you among those I love and diminish you among those I hate.” Ibn Abi Nujayh said: Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr told him on the authority of Mujahid who said: It was said that the Nun is the great whale that is under the seventh earth. Al-Baghawi and a group of commentators mentioned that on the back of this whale is a rock as thick as the heavens and the earth, and on its back is a bull with forty thousand horns, and on its back are the seven earths and what is in them and what is between them, and God knows best. It is strange that some of them interpreted this meaning of the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Ismail told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas that Abdullah bin Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, so he came to him and asked him about some things. He said, I am going to ask you about things that only a prophet knows. He said, What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food that the people of Paradise will eat? Why does the child gravitate toward his father? Why does the child gravitate toward his mother? He said, Gabriel told me about them just now. Ibn Salam said, That is the enemy of the Jews from the angels. He said, “As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather them from the east to the west, and the first food that the people of Paradise will eat is the extra liver of a fish. As for the child, if the man’s semen precedes the woman’s semen, the child will be born, and if the woman’s semen precedes the man’s semen, the woman will be born.” Al-Bukhari narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Hamid, and Muslim also narrated it. He has a hadith from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to this. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Asma’ al-Rahbi, on the authority of Thawban, “A rabbi asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, On issues, one of which was that he said: “What is their gift?” meaning the people of Paradise when they enter Paradise? He said: The extra liver of a whale. He said: What is their food after that? He said: The bull of Paradise that used to eat from its edges will be slaughtered for them. He said: What is their drink after that? He said: From a spring in it called Salsabil. It was said that what is meant by his saying: N is a tablet of light. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan bin Shabib Al-Maktab narrated to us, Muhammad bin Ziyad Al-Jazari narrated to us, on the authority of Furat bin Abi Al-Furat, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurrah, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Nun. By the Pen and what they write.’ A tablet of light and a pen of light that records what will be until the Day of Resurrection.” This is a strange mursal narration. Ibn Jurayj said: I was told that that pen of light is one hundred years long. It was said that what is meant by his saying Nun is an inkwell, and the pen is the pen. Ibn Jarir said: Abd Al-A’la narrated to us, Abu Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Qatadah, regarding his saying Nun, they said that it is the inkwell. A very strange hadith has been narrated in this regard, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham bin Khalid narrated to us, Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, Abu Abdullah, the client of the Umayyads, narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God created the nun, and it is the inkwell. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yaqub told us, my brother Isa bin Abdullah told us, Thabit Ath-Thamali told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God created the inkwell, and created the pen, and said: Write. He said: What should I write? He said: Write everything that will occur until the Day of Resurrection of deeds done righteous or wicked, or allocated provision, lawful or unlawful. Then He made everything of that obligatory in its nature, its entry into this world, its duration in it, and its exit from it. Then He appointed guardians over the servants and keepers of the Book. The guardians copy from the guardians every day the deeds of that day. Then when the provision is exhausted, the record is cut off, and the appointed time has passed, the guardians come to the keepers asking for the deeds of that day. The guardians say to them: We do not find anything for your companion with us. Then the guardians return and find that they have died. Ibn Abbas said: Are you not an Arab people who hear the guardians say: We used to copy what you used to do. And can copying be anything other than from an original? God the Almighty said: And the pen apparently refers to the same type of pen that is used to write, as in His statement: Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous * Who taught by the pen * Taught man that which he knew not. So it is an oath from Him the Almighty and a reminder to His creation of the blessing He bestowed upon them of learning to write by which knowledge is attained. For this reason He said: and what they inscribe Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: It means what they write. Abu Ad-Dhaha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: and what they inscribe means what they do. As-Suddi said: and what they inscribe means the angels and what they write of the deeds of the servants. Others said: Rather, what is meant here is the pen that God made move by decree when He wrote down the destinies of creation, fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. They mentioned in this regard the hadiths that mention the pen. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed bin Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan and Yunus bin Habib told us: Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi told us, Abdul Wahid bin Salim Al-Sulami told us, on the authority of Ata’, who is Ibn Abi Rabah, Al-Walid bin Ubadah bin Al-Samit told me: My father called me when death was approaching him and said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it, ‘Write.’ It said, ‘O Lord, what should I write?’ It said, ‘Write the destiny and what will be forever.’” This hadith was narrated by Imam Ahmad through various chains of narration on the authority of Al-Walid bin Ubadah on the authority of his father on this authority. Al-Tirmidhi included it on the authority of Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi on this authority, and he said, It is hasan saheeh ghareeb. It was narrated by Abu Dawud in his book, As-Sunnah, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Musafir, on the authority of Yahya ibn Hassan, on the authority of Ibn Rabah, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubla, on the authority of Abu Hafsah, whose name was Habish ibn Shuraih Al-Habashi Ash-Shami, on the authority of Ubadah, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah At-Tusi told us, Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq told us, Abdullah ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Rabah ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Habib, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to narrate that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The first thing that God created was the pen, and He commanded it to write everything. This is strange from this chain of narration, and they did not include it. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: The pen means that with which the remembrance is written. And the statement of God, and what they inscribe means what they write, as mentioned above. His statement: You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman means, praise be to God, you are not a madman as the ignorant among your people say, who deny the guidance and clear truth that you have brought them, and they attribute madness to you because of it. And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted means, rather, for you is a great reward and a bountiful recompense that does not cease or perish for conveying the message of your Lord to creation and your patience in the face of their harm. The meaning of uninterrupted is not cut off like His statement, a gift that is not cut off, so for them is a reward uninterrupted meaning, it is not cut off from them. Mujahid said: uninterrupted means not counted, and this goes back to what we have said. God the Almighty says: {And indeed, you are of a great moral character}. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: {And indeed, you are of a great religion, which is Islam}. Mujahid, Abu Malik, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said the same, as did Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd. Atiyyah said: {And indeed, you are of great manners}. Muammar said on the authority of Qatadah: Aisha was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {His character was the Qur’an}. She said as it is in the Qur’an. Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba said on the authority of Qatadah regarding His statement: {And indeed, you are of a great moral character}. It was mentioned to us that Sa’d ibn Hisham asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {Do you not recite the Qur’an?} He said: {Yes}. She said: {The character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the Qur’an}. Abdur-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Zurara ibn Awfa on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham who said: I asked Aisha and said: {Tell me, O Mother of the Believers, about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {Do you recite the Qur’an?} I said: {Yes}. She said: {His character was the Qur’an}. This is an abbreviation of a long hadith. Imam Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Qatada in full, and it will come in Surat Al-Muzzammil, God willing, and he is trustworthy. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and she said: His character was the Qur’an. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Wahb, on the authority of a man from Banu Sawad, who said: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and she said: Do you not recite the Qur’an? And indeed, you are of a great moral character. He said: I said: Tell me about that. She said: I made him food and Hafsah made him food, and I said to my slave girl, Go, and if she brings the food and sets it down before me, throw the food away. She said: So she brought the food, and the slave girl threw it, and the bowl fell and broke, and it was a cutlery. She said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) gathered it and said: Retrieve - or Aswad was unsure - Retrieve - a container in place of your container. She said: So he did not say anything. Ibn Jarir said: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Al-Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham, who said: I came to Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, and said to her: Tell me about the character of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: His character was the Qur’an. Do you not read: And indeed, you are of a great moral character? Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated something similar from the hadith of Al-Hasan. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Mu’awiyah ibn Salih informed me, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahriyyah, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: I performed Hajj and went to Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and asked her about the character of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: The character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Qur’an. Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, and An-Nasa’i narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Ishaq ibn Mansur, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Salih, with this same chain of transmission. This means that, peace and blessings be upon him, obeying the Quran’s commands and prohibitions became his nature, a characteristic that was inherent in him, and he abandoned his innate nature. Whatever the Quran commanded him to do, he did, and whatever it forbade him from doing, he abandoned. This was in addition to the great character traits that God created in him, such as modesty, generosity, courage, forgiveness, and patience, and every beautiful character trait, as proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Anas, who said: I served the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, for ten years, and he never once said to me uff, nor did he say about something I did, Why did you do that? nor about something I did not do, Why didn’t you do that? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the best of people in character. I have never touched silk or brocade or anything softer than the hand of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), nor have I smelled musk or perfume that was more fragrant than the sweat of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq bin Mansur told us, Ibrahim bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Al-Bara’ say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) had the most handsome face and the best character. He was neither tall nor short. There are many hadiths on this. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi has a book on this in his book Al-Shama’il. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never struck a servant of his with his hand, nor did he strike a woman, nor did he strike anything with his hand except when he was fighting in the cause of God. He never gave a choice between two things except that the lesser of the two was more beloved to him, until it was a sin. But if it was a sin, he was the furthest of people from sin. He never took revenge for himself from something that was done to him, except when the sacred limits of God were violated, in which case he would take revenge for the sake of God, the Almighty and Majestic. Imam Ahmad said: Saeed ibn Mansur told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, on the authority of al-Qa’qa’ ibn Hakim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was only sent to perfect good character. He is the only one who transmitted it. And the saying of God the Almighty: Then you will see, and they will see * Which of you is the one who is afflicted. So you will know, O Muhammad, and your opponents and those who deny you will know who is the one who is afflicted and misguided among you and among them. This is like His saying the Almighty: They will know tomorrow who is the most evil liar. And His saying the Almighty: And either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said about this verse, You will know, and they will know on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Which of you is afflicted means the insane. Mujahid and others said the same. Qatadah and others said: Which of you is afflicted means the most deserving of Satan. The meaning of the one who is afflicted is clear: the one who has been afflicted and has gone astray from the truth. The preposition with was added to His saying which of you to indicate the inclusion of the verb in His saying Then you will see, and they will see. The meaning is: You will know, and they will know, or You will inform, and they will inform, which of you is the one who is afflicted. And God knows best. Then God Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided. That is, He, the Almighty, knows which of the two groups among you is the one who is guided, and He knows which party has strayed from the truth.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah At-Tusi told us, Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq told us, Abdullah ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Rabah ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Habib, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to narrate that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The first thing that God created was the pen, and He commanded it to write everything. This is strange from this chain of narration, and they did not include it. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: The pen means that with which the remembrance is written. And the statement of God, and what they inscribe means what they write, as mentioned above. His statement: You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman means, praise be to God, you are not a madman as the ignorant among your people say, who deny the guidance and clear truth that you have brought them, and they attribute madness to you because of it. And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted means, rather, for you is a great reward and a bountiful recompense that does not cease or perish for conveying the message of your Lord to creation and your patience in the face of their harm. The meaning of uninterrupted is not cut off like His statement, a gift that is not cut off, so for them is a reward uninterrupted meaning, it is not cut off from them. Mujahid said: uninterrupted means not counted, and this goes back to what we have said. God the Almighty says: {And indeed, you are of a great moral character}. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: {And indeed, you are of a great religion, which is Islam}. Mujahid, Abu Malik, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said the same, as did Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd. Atiyyah said: {And indeed, you are of great manners}. Muammar said on the authority of Qatadah: Aisha was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {His character was the Qur’an}. She said as it is in the Qur’an. Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba said on the authority of Qatadah regarding His statement: {And indeed, you are of a great moral character}. It was mentioned to us that Sa’d ibn Hisham asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {Do you not recite the Qur’an?} He said: {Yes}. She said: {The character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the Qur’an}. Abdur-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Zurara ibn Awfa on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham who said: I asked Aisha and said: {Tell me, O Mother of the Believers, about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {Do you recite the Qur’an?} I said: {Yes}. She said: {His character was the Qur’an}. This is an abbreviation of a long hadith. Imam Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Qatada in full, and it will come in Surat Al-Muzzammil, God willing, and he is trustworthy. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and she said: His character was the Qur’an. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Wahb, on the authority of a man from Banu Sawad, who said: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and she said: Do you not recite the Qur’an? And indeed, you are of a great moral character. He said: I said: Tell me about that. She said: I made him food and Hafsah made him food, and I said to my slave girl, Go, and if she brings the food and sets it down before me, throw the food away. She said: So she brought the food, and the slave girl threw it, and the bowl fell and broke, and it was a cutlery. She said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) gathered it and said: Retrieve - or Aswad was unsure - Retrieve - a container in place of your container. She said: So he did not say anything. Ibn Jarir said: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Al-Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham, who said: I came to Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, and said to her: Tell me about the character of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: His character was the Qur’an. Do you not read: And indeed, you are of a great moral character? Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated something similar from the hadith of Al-Hasan. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Mu’awiyah ibn Salih informed me, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahriyyah, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: I performed Hajj and went to Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and asked her about the character of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: The character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Qur’an. Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, and An-Nasa’i narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Ishaq ibn Mansur, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Salih, with this same chain of transmission. This means that, peace and blessings be upon him, obeying the Quran’s commands and prohibitions became his nature, a characteristic that was inherent in him, and he abandoned his innate nature. Whatever the Quran commanded him to do, he did, and whatever it forbade him from doing, he abandoned. This was in addition to the great character traits that God created in him, such as modesty, generosity, courage, forgiveness, and patience, and every beautiful character trait, as proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Anas, who said: I served the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, for ten years, and he never once said to me uff, nor did he say about something I did, Why did you do that? nor about something I did not do, Why didn’t you do that? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the best of people in character. I have never touched silk or brocade or anything softer than the hand of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), nor have I smelled musk or perfume that was more fragrant than the sweat of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq bin Mansur told us, Ibrahim bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Al-Bara’ say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) had the most handsome face and the best character. He was neither tall nor short. There are many hadiths on this. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi has a book on this in his book Al-Shama’il. He never gave a choice between two things except that the lesser of the two was more beloved to him, until it was a sin. But if it was a sin, he was the furthest of people from sin. He never took revenge for himself from something that was done to him, except when the sacred limits of God were violated, in which case he would take revenge for the sake of God, the Almighty and Majestic. Imam Ahmad said: Saeed ibn Mansur told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, on the authority of al-Qa’qa’ ibn Hakim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was only sent to perfect good character. He is the only one who transmitted it. And the saying of God the Almighty: Then you will see, and they will see * Which of you is the one who is afflicted. So you will know, O Muhammad, and your opponents and those who deny you will know who is the one who is afflicted and misguided among you and among them. This is like His saying the Almighty: They will know tomorrow who is the most evil liar. And His saying the Almighty: And either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said about this verse, You will know, and they will know on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Which of you is afflicted means the insane. Mujahid and others said the same. Qatadah and others said: Which of you is afflicted means the most deserving of Satan. The meaning of the one who is afflicted is clear: the one who has been afflicted and has gone astray from the truth. The preposition with was added to His saying which of you to indicate the inclusion of the verb in His saying Then you will see, and they will see. The meaning is: You will know, and they will know, or You will inform, and they will inform, which of you is the one who is afflicted. And God knows best. Then God Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided. That is, He, the Almighty, knows which of the two groups among you is the one who is guided, and He knows which party has strayed from the truth.
68:6: We have already discussed the letters of the alphabet at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, and that the Almighty’s saying: Nun is like His saying Sad, “Qaf,” and similar disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs. The explanation of that is clearer than repeating it here. It was said: What is meant by the saying Nun is a great whale on the great, surrounding current of water, and it carries the seven earths, as Imam Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan - he is Al-Thawri - told us, Sulayman - he is Al-A’mash - told us, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing that God created was the pen. He said: Write. He said: What should I write? He said: Write down the destiny. So he wrote down what would happen from that day until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the Noon and raised the water vapor, from which the heavens burst forth and the earth was spread out on the back of the Noon. The Noon shook and the earth shook and was fixed with mountains, so they stand tall on the earth. And thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Sinan on the authority of Abu Muawiyah on the authority of Al-A’mash on his authority. And thus Shu’bah, Muhammad ibn Fadil, and Waki’ narrated it on the authority of Al-A’mash on his authority. And Shu`bah added in his narration, then he recited, “Nun. By the pen and what they write.” Sharik narrated it on the authority of Al-A`mash on the authority of Abu Dhibyan or Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so he mentioned something similar to it. Mu`mar narrated it on the authority of Al-A`mash that Ibn Abbas said: So he mentioned it, then he recited, “Nun. By the pen and what they write.” Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, created was the pen, then He said to it: Write, so it wrote what will be until the Hour comes, then He created the nun above the water, then He pressed the earth down upon it. Al-Tabarani narrated this with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: Abu Habib Zaid bin Al-Mahdi Al-Marwazi told us, Saeed bin Yaqub Al-Talaqani told us, Muammil bin Ismail told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha Muslim bin Subaih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first thing God created was the Pen and the Whale. Then He said to al-Qalam 68:Write. It said: What should I write? He said: Everything will be until the Day of Resurrection.” Then he recited: “Nun. By the Pen and what they inscribe.” So the Nun is the Whale, and the Pen is the Pen. Another hadith on this was narrated by Ibn Asakir on the authority of Abu Abdullah, the client of the Umayyads, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first thing God created was the pen. Then He created the nun, which is the inkwell. Then He said to it: Write. It said: What should I write? He said: Write what will be - or what will be - of deeds, provision, effect, or lifespan. So He wrote that until the Day of Resurrection. This is His saying: ‘Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.’ Then He sealed the pen, so it did not speak until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the intellect and said: By My glory, I will perfect you among those I love and diminish you among those I hate.” Ibn Abi Nujayh said: Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr told him on the authority of Mujahid who said: It was said that the Nun is the great whale that is under the seventh earth. Al-Baghawi and a group of commentators mentioned that on the back of this whale is a rock as thick as the heavens and the earth, and on its back is a bull with forty thousand horns, and on its back are the seven earths and what is in them and what is between them, and God knows best. It is strange that some of them interpreted this meaning of the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Ismail told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas that Abdullah bin Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, so he came to him and asked him about some things. He said, I am going to ask you about things that only a prophet knows. He said, What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food that the people of Paradise will eat? Why does the child gravitate toward his father? Why does the child gravitate toward his mother? He said, Gabriel told me about them just now. Ibn Salam said, That is the enemy of the Jews from the angels. He said, “As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather them from the east to the west, and the first food that the people of Paradise will eat is the extra liver of a fish. As for the child, if the man’s semen precedes the woman’s semen, the child will be born, and if the woman’s semen precedes the man’s semen, the woman will be born.” Al-Bukhari narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Hamid, and Muslim also narrated it. He has a hadith from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to this. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Asma’ al-Rahbi, on the authority of Thawban, “A rabbi asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, On issues, one of which was that he said: “What is their gift?” meaning the people of Paradise when they enter Paradise? He said: What is their drink after that? He said: From a spring in it called Salsabil. It was said that what is meant by his saying: N is a tablet of light. The meaning of the one who is afflicted is clear: the one who has been afflicted and has gone astray from the truth. The preposition with was added to His saying which of you to indicate the inclusion of the verb in His saying Then you will see, and they will see. The meaning is: You will know, and they will know, or You will inform, and they will inform, which of you is the one who is afflicted. And God knows best. Then God Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided. That is, He, the Almighty, knows which of the two groups among you is the one who is guided, and He knows which party has strayed from the truth.
68:7: We have already discussed the letters of the alphabet at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, and that the Almighty’s saying: Nun is like His saying Sad, “Qaf,” and similar disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs. The explanation of that is clearer than repeating it here. It was said: What is meant by the saying Nun is a great whale on the great, surrounding current of water, and it carries the seven earths, as Imam Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan - he is Al-Thawri - told us, Sulayman - he is Al-A’mash - told us, on the authority of Abu Dhibyan - on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing that God created was the pen. He said: Write. He said: What should I write? He said: Write down the destiny. So he wrote down what would happen from that day until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the Noon and raised the water vapor, from which the heavens burst forth and the earth was spread out on the back of the Noon. The Noon shook and the earth shook and was fixed with mountains, so they stand tall on the earth. And thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Sinan on the authority of Abu Muawiyah on the authority of Al-A’mash on his authority. And thus Shu’bah, Muhammad ibn Fadil, and Waki’ narrated it on the authority of Al-A’mash on his authority. And Shu`bah added in his narration, then he recited, “Nun. By the pen and what they write.” Sharik narrated it on the authority of Al-A`mash on the authority of Abu Dhibyan or Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so he mentioned something similar to it. Mu`mar narrated it on the authority of Al-A`mash that Ibn Abbas said: So he mentioned it, then he recited, “Nun. By the pen and what they write.” Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, created was the pen, then He said to it: Write, so it wrote what will be until the Hour comes, then He created the nun above the water, then He pressed the earth down upon it. Al-Tabarani narrated this with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: Abu Habib Zaid bin Al-Mahdi Al-Marwazi told us, Saeed bin Yaqub Al-Talaqani told us, Muammil bin Ismail told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha Muslim bin Subaih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first thing God created was the Pen and the Whale. Then He said to al-Qalam 68:Write. It said: What should I write? He said: Everything will be until the Day of Resurrection.” Then he recited: “Nun. By the Pen and what they inscribe.” So the Nun is the Whale, and the Pen is the Pen. Another hadith on this was narrated by Ibn Asakir on the authority of Abu Abdullah, the client of the Umayyads, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first thing God created was the pen. Then He created the nun, which is the inkwell. Then He said to it: Write. It said: What should I write? He said: Write what will be - or what will be - of deeds, provision, effect, or lifespan. So He wrote that until the Day of Resurrection. This is His saying: ‘Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.’ Then He sealed the pen, so it did not speak until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the intellect and said: By My glory, I will perfect you among those I love and diminish you among those I hate.” Ibn Abi Nujayh said: Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr told him on the authority of Mujahid who said: It was said that the Nun is the great whale that is under the seventh earth. Al-Baghawi and a group of commentators mentioned that on the back of this whale is a rock as thick as the heavens and the earth, and on its back is a bull with forty thousand horns, and on its back are the seven earths and what is in them and what is between them, and God knows best. It is strange that some of them interpreted this meaning of the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Ismail told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas that Abdullah bin Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, so he came to him and asked him about some things. He said, I am going to ask you about things that only a prophet knows. He said, What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food that the people of Paradise will eat? Why does the child gravitate toward his father? Why does the child gravitate toward his mother? He said, Gabriel told me about them just now. Ibn Salam said, That is the enemy of the Jews from the angels. He said, “As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather them from the east to the west, and the first food that the people of Paradise will eat is the extra liver of a fish. As for the child, if the man’s semen precedes the woman’s semen, the child will be born, and if the woman’s semen precedes the man’s semen, the woman will be born.” Al-Bukhari narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Hamid, and Muslim also narrated it. He has a hadith from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to this. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Asma’ al-Rahbi, on the authority of Thawban, “A rabbi asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, On issues, one of which was that he said: “What is their gift?” meaning the people of Paradise when they enter Paradise? He said: The extra liver of a whale. He said: What is their food after that? He said: The bull of Paradise that used to eat from its edges will be slaughtered for them. He said: What is their drink after that? He said: From a spring in it called Salsabil. It was said that what is meant by his saying: N is a tablet of light. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan bin Shabib Al-Maktab narrated to us, Muhammad bin Ziyad Al-Jazari narrated to us, on the authority of Furat bin Abi Al-Furat, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurrah, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Nun. By the Pen and what they write.’ A tablet of light and a pen of light that records what will be until the Day of Resurrection.” This is a strange mursal narration. Ibn Jurayj said: I was told that that pen of light is one hundred years long. It was said that what is meant by his saying Nun is an inkwell, and the pen is the pen. Ibn Jarir said: Abd Al-A’la narrated to us, Abu Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Qatadah, regarding his saying Nun, they said that it is the inkwell. A very strange hadith has been narrated in this regard, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham bin Khalid narrated to us, Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, Abu Abdullah, the client of the Umayyads, narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God created the nun, and it is the inkwell. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yaqub told us, my brother Isa bin Abdullah told us, Thabit Ath-Thamali told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God created the inkwell, and created the pen, and said: Write. He said: What should I write? He said: Write everything that will occur until the Day of Resurrection of deeds done righteous or wicked, or allocated provision, lawful or unlawful. Then He made everything of that obligatory in its nature, its entry into this world, its duration in it, and its exit from it. Then He appointed guardians over the servants and keepers of the Book. The guardians copy from the guardians every day the deeds of that day. Then when the provision is exhausted, the record is cut off, and the appointed time has passed, the guardians come to the keepers asking for the deeds of that day. The guardians say to them: We do not find anything for your companion with us. Then the guardians return and find that they have died. Ibn Abbas said: Are you not an Arab people who hear the guardians say: We used to copy what you used to do. And can copying be anything other than from an original? God the Almighty said: And the pen apparently refers to the same type of pen that is used to write, as in His statement: Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous * Who taught by the pen * Taught man that which he knew not. So it is an oath from Him the Almighty and a reminder to His creation of the blessing He bestowed upon them of learning to write by which knowledge is attained. For this reason He said: and what they inscribe Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: It means what they write. Abu Ad-Dhaha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: and what they inscribe means what they do. As-Suddi said: and what they inscribe means the angels and what they write of the deeds of the servants. Others said: Rather, what is meant here is the pen that God made move by decree when He wrote down the destinies of creation, fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. They mentioned in this regard the hadiths that mention the pen. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed bin Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan and Yunus bin Habib told us: Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi told us, Abdul Wahid bin Salim Al-Sulami told us, on the authority of Ata’, who is Ibn Abi Rabah, Al-Walid bin Ubadah bin Al-Samit told me: My father called me when death was approaching him and said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first thing God created was the pen. He said to it, ‘Write.’ It said, ‘O Lord, what should I write?’ It said, ‘Write the destiny and what will be forever.’” This hadith was narrated by Imam Ahmad through various chains of narration on the authority of Al-Walid bin Ubadah on the authority of his father on this authority. Al-Tirmidhi included it on the authority of Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi on this authority, and he said, It is hasan saheeh ghareeb. It was narrated by Abu Dawud in his book, As-Sunnah, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Musafir, on the authority of Yahya ibn Hassan, on the authority of Ibn Rabah, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubla, on the authority of Abu Hafsah, whose name was Habish ibn Shuraih Al-Habashi Ash-Shami, on the authority of Ubadah, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah At-Tusi told us, Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq told us, Abdullah ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Rabah ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Habib, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to narrate that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The first thing that God created was the pen, and He commanded it to write everything. This is strange from this chain of narration, and they did not include it. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: The pen means that with which the remembrance is written. And the statement of God, and what they inscribe means what they write, as mentioned above. His statement: You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman means, praise be to God, you are not a madman as the ignorant among your people say, who deny the guidance and clear truth that you have brought them, and they attribute madness to you because of it. And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted means, rather, for you is a great reward and a bountiful recompense that does not cease or perish for conveying the message of your Lord to creation and your patience in the face of their harm. The meaning of uninterrupted is not cut off like His statement, a gift that is not cut off, so for them is a reward uninterrupted meaning, it is not cut off from them. Mujahid said: uninterrupted means not counted, and this goes back to what we have said. God the Almighty says: {And indeed, you are of a great moral character}. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: {And indeed, you are of a great religion, which is Islam}. Mujahid, Abu Malik, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said the same, as did Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd. Atiyyah said: {And indeed, you are of great manners}. Muammar said on the authority of Qatadah: Aisha was asked about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {His character was the Qur’an}. She said as it is in the Qur’an. Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba said on the authority of Qatadah regarding His statement: {And indeed, you are of a great moral character}. It was mentioned to us that Sa’d ibn Hisham asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {Do you not recite the Qur’an?} He said: {Yes}. She said: {The character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the Qur’an}. Abdur-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Zurara ibn Awfa on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham who said: I asked Aisha and said: {Tell me, O Mother of the Believers, about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She said: {Do you recite the Qur’an?} I said: {Yes}. She said: {His character was the Qur’an}. This is an abbreviation of a long hadith. Imam Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Qatada in full, and it will come in Surat Al-Muzzammil, God willing, and he is trustworthy. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and she said: His character was the Qur’an. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Wahb, on the authority of a man from Banu Sawad, who said: I asked Aisha about the character of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and she said: Do you not recite the Qur’an? And indeed, you are of a great moral character. He said: I said: Tell me about that. She said: I made him food and Hafsah made him food, and I said to my slave girl, Go, and if she brings the food and sets it down before me, throw the food away. She said: So she brought the food, and the slave girl threw it, and the bowl fell and broke, and it was a cutlery. She said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) gathered it and said: Retrieve - or Aswad was unsure - Retrieve - a container in place of your container. She said: So he did not say anything. Ibn Jarir said: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Al-Mubarak ibn Fadalah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham, who said: I came to Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, and said to her: Tell me about the character of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: His character was the Qur’an. Do you not read: And indeed, you are of a great moral character? Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated something similar from the hadith of Al-Hasan. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Mu’awiyah ibn Salih informed me, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahriyyah, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr, who said: I performed Hajj and went to Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and asked her about the character of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: The character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Qur’an. Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, and An-Nasa’i narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Ishaq ibn Mansur, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Salih, with this same chain of transmission. This means that, peace and blessings be upon him, obeying the Quran’s commands and prohibitions became his nature, a characteristic that was inherent in him, and he abandoned his innate nature. Whatever the Quran commanded him to do, he did, and whatever it forbade him from doing, he abandoned. This was in addition to the great character traits that God created in him, such as modesty, generosity, courage, forgiveness, and patience, and every beautiful character trait, as proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Anas, who said: I served the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, for ten years, and he never once said to me uff, nor did he say about something I did, Why did you do that? nor about something I did not do, Why didn’t you do that? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was the best of people in character. I have never touched silk or brocade or anything softer than the hand of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), nor have I smelled musk or perfume that was more fragrant than the sweat of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq bin Mansur told us, Ibrahim bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Al-Bara’ say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) had the most handsome face and the best character. He was neither tall nor short. There are many hadiths on this. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi has a book on this in his book Al-Shama’il. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never struck a servant of his with his hand, nor did he strike a woman, nor did he strike anything with his hand except when he was fighting in the cause of God. He never gave a choice between two things except that the lesser of the two was more beloved to him, until it was a sin. But if it was a sin, he was the furthest of people from sin. He never took revenge for himself from something that was done to him, except when the sacred limits of God were violated, in which case he would take revenge for the sake of God, the Almighty and Majestic. Imam Ahmad said: Saeed ibn Mansur told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, on the authority of al-Qa’qa’ ibn Hakim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was only sent to perfect good character. He is the only one who transmitted it. And the saying of God the Almighty: Then you will see, and they will see * Which of you is the one who is afflicted. So you will know, O Muhammad, and your opponents and those who deny you will know who is the one who is afflicted and misguided among you and among them. This is like His saying the Almighty: They will know tomorrow who is the most evil liar. And His saying the Almighty: And either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said about this verse, You will know, and they will know on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Which of you is afflicted means the insane. Mujahid and others said the same. Qatadah and others said: Which of you is afflicted means the most deserving of Satan. The meaning of the one who is afflicted is clear: the one who has been afflicted and has gone astray from the truth. The preposition with was added to His saying which of you to indicate the inclusion of the verb in His saying Then you will see, and they will see. The meaning is: You will know, and they will know, or You will inform, and they will inform, which of you is the one who is afflicted. And God knows best. Then God Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided. That is, He, the Almighty, knows which of the two groups among you is the one who is guided, and He knows which party has strayed from the truth.
68:8: God the Almighty says: “As We have bestowed upon you blessings and given you the straight law and the great character, “So do not obey the deniers. They wish that you would compromise, so they would compromise.” Ibn Abbas said: If you were to make concessions to them, they would make concessions. Mujahid said: They wish that you would compromise means that you would bow to their gods and abandon the truth that you are upon. Then God the Almighty said: And do not obey every insignificant swearer. That is because the liar, due to his weakness and insignificance, is protected by his false oaths, by which he dares to use the names of God the Almighty and to use them all the time out of place. Ibn Abbas said: The insignificant one is the liar. Mujahid said: He is the weak-hearted one. Al-Hasan said: Every stubborn, insignificant, and weak swearer. God the Almighty said: A slanderer Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: It means backbiting. Wandering about with tales means the one who walks among people, sows discord between them and spreads gossip to corrupt relations, which is the razor. It has been proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Mujahid from Tawus from Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) passed by two graves and said: “They are being punished, but they are not being punished for a major sin. As for one of them, he did not protect himself from urine, and as for the other, he used to walk about with tales” The rest of the group narrated it in their books from various chains of narration on the authority of Mujahid. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam, that Hudhayfah said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: A gossiper will not enter Paradise. This was narrated by all except Ibn Majah through various chains of narration on the authority of Ibrahim. Abd al-Razzaq told us, Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: A gossiper will not enter Paradise, meaning a slanderer. Yahya ibn Sa’id al-Qattan told me, Abu Sa’id al-Ahwal told us, on the authority of al-A’mash. Ibrahim told me about sixty years ago, on the authority of Hammam ibn al-Harith, who said: A man passed by Hudhayfah, and it was said that this man conveys hadith to the rulers. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, or he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A gossiper will not enter Paradise. Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Mahdi told us, on the authority of Wasil al-Ahdab, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, who said: Hudhayfah heard that a man was a gossiper, so he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: A gossiper will not enter Paradise. Gossiper. Imam Ahmad said: Abdur-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Khathim, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Asma’ bint Yazid ibn As-Sakn, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not tell you about the best of you? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Those who, when they are seen, remind God of His praise. Then he said: Shall I not tell you about the worst of you? Those who go about spreading gossip, causing trouble between loved ones, and seeking to harm the innocent. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Suwayd ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Yahya ibn Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Khathim, on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Husayn, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abdur-Rahman ibn Ghanam, conveying it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The best of God’s servants are those who, when they are seen, remind God of His praise. The worst of God’s servants are those who go about spreading gossip, causing division between loved ones, and seeking to harm the innocent.” God the Almighty said: He who prevents good, is an aggressor, a sinner. That is, he prevents what is due from him and what he has of good. Aggressor in consuming what God has permitted him, exceeding the permissible limit. Athim means he consumes forbidden things. God the Almighty said: He became violent after that, a fornicator. As for atil, it is the rude, coarse, sound, plural, and varied. Imam Ahmad said: “Waki’ and Abdurrahman narrated to us from Sufyan from Ma’bad ibn Khalid from Haritha ibn Wahb who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Shall I not inform you of the people of Paradise? Every weak and oppressed one, if he swears an oath by God, He will fulfill it. Shall I not inform you of the people of Hellfire? Every violent, arrogant one.” Waki’ said: Every violent, arrogant, and haughty one. They both included it in their Sahihs and the rest of the group except Abu Dawud from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu’bah, both from Sa’id ibn Khalid with it. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Abd al-Rahman told us, Musa ibn Ali told us: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-Aas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when mentioning the people of Hell: Everyone is arrogant, haughty, and stubborn. Ahmad alone transmitted this. Linguists say: Al-Ja'zari is the rough and coarse one. And Al-Jawaz is the diverse and plural one. Imam Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us, `Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanim, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about the `atil zanim, and he said: He is the one who is harsh in nature, healthy, a glutton, a drinker, who has enough food and drink, oppressive to people, and generous in stomach. With this chain of transmission, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The greedy, stubborn, ignorant, ignorant will not enter Paradise. More than one of the Tabi`un also transmitted it in a mursal. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn `Abd al-A`la narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Thawr, on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The heavens weep over a servant whose body God has made healthy, whose stomach is generous, and to whom He has given a portion of this world, yet he oppresses people. He said: That is the `atil zanim.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in this way through two mursal chains of transmission, and more than one of the Salaf has explicitly stated this, including Mujahid, `Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others, that the `atil is the one who is well-mannered, strong in eating, drinking, fornication, and other things. As for the zanim, he said: Al-Bukhari: Mahmoud told us, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He became a stubborn, ungrateful man after that. He said: A man from Quraysh who had a tail like the tail of a sheep. The meaning of this is that he was famous for his evil, like the fame of a sheep with a tail among its sisters. Rather, the ungrateful man in the language of the Arabs is the one who is called a heretic among the people. Ibn Jarir and more than one of the imams said this. He said: And from this is the saying of Hassan bin Thabit, meaning he is criticizing some of the infidels of Quraysh: You are a bastard who has been hung on the Hashimites as a single cup is hung behind a rider. Another said: A bastard who does not know who his father is, a prostitute whose mother is a lowly man Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ammar bin Khalid Al-Wasiti told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Zanim, he said: The vulgar, mean, immoral, ignoble person. Then Ibn Abbas said: A fornicator who is called by men increases as the width of the legs increases Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The fornicator is the called one. It is said that the fornicator is a man who has a known affliction. It is said that he is Al-Akhns bin Shuraik Al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhrah. Some people from Banu Zuhrah claimed that the fornicator was Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth Al-Zuhri, but he was not him. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he claimed that the fornicator is the one whose lineage is attributed. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the scholars of tafsir, they said: He is the one who has a hump like the hump of a sheep. It was said that its meaning is, Their middle one said, ‘Did I not tell you, why do you not glorify God?’ That is, why do you not glorify God and thank Him for what He has given you and bestowed upon you? For this reason, they said, Indeed, we were wrongdoers. So some of them turned to others, blaming each other for what they had insisted on of preventing the poor from receiving the right to collect the crops. So the only response of some of them to others was to admit the sin and guilt. They said, ‘Woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors.’ That is, we transgressed and transgressed. We were arrogant and crossed the line until what happened to us happened to us. "Perhaps our Lord will give us in exchange [for something] better than it. Indeed, we are desirous of our Lord." 68:34: When God the Almighty mentioned the state of the people of the earthly Paradise and the punishment that befell them therein when they disobeyed God the Almighty and disobeyed His command, He explained that for those who fear Him and obey Him, there are gardens of bliss in the Hereafter that will never perish, never empty, and whose bliss will never end. Then God the Almighty said: Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals? That is, shall We treat these people equally in recompense? No, by the Lord of the earth and the heavens. That is why He said: What is the matter with you? How do you judge? That is, how do you think that? Then God the Almighty said: Or do you have a Book in which you study? * Indeed, you will have therein whatever you choose. God the Almighty says: “Is there in your hands a Book sent down from the heaven which you study, memorize, and circulate through the transmission of generations from generation to generation, containing a definite ruling, as you claim?” “Indeed, you will have therein whatever you choose. * Or have you oaths from Us binding until the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, you will have whatever you judge.” That is, do you have covenants and definite agreements from Us? Indeed, you will have whatever you judge. That is, do you have pledges from Us and definite agreements? Indeed, you will have whatever you judge. That is, you will get what you want and desire. Ask them which of them is responsible for that. That is, tell them who is the one who guarantees it? Ibn Abbas said: He says which of them is responsible for that. Or do they have partners? That is, from idols and rivals. Then let them produce their partners, if they should be truthful.
