Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir narrated all of this, then he said, Abu Zayd `Umar ibn Shabah told me, Harun ibn `Umar Al-Makhzumi told us, Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, Abu Sa`id Ruh ibn Janah told us, on the authority of a client of `Umar ibn `Abd Al-`Aziz, on the authority of Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, On the Day the shin is laid bare, meaning a great light before which they prostrate themselves. Abu Ya`la narrated it on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, on the authority of Al-Walid ibn Muslim, with it, and in it is a man. It is unclear, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: Their eyes will be humbled, humiliation will cover them meaning in the Hereafter because of their crimes and arrogance in this world, so they were punished with the opposite of what they were doing. And when they were called to prostrate in this world and refused to do so despite their good health and safety, likewise they will be punished with their inability to do so in the Hereafter. When the Lord Almighty appears, the believers will prostrate to Him, and none of the disbelievers or hypocrites will be able to prostrate. Rather, their backs will return to being level, and whenever one of them wants to prostrate, he will fall on his back, the opposite of prostration, as they were in this world, unlike what the believers are doing. Then God the Almighty said: So leave Me and him who denies this statement, meaning the Qur’an. This is a severe threat, meaning leave Me and him, for I know more about it than he does how to lure him and extend his error and give him respite, then I will seize him with the grasp of the Mighty, the Powerful. For this reason God the Almighty said: We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know, meaning while they are unaware, rather they believe that this is an honor from God, while in reality it is an insult, as God the Almighty said: Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children * We hasten to them with good things? Rather, they do not perceive. And God the Almighty said: “But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the gates of every [good] thing until, just as they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair.” For this reason He said here: “And grant them respite. Indeed, My plan is firm,” meaning I will delay them, give them respite, and grant them respite. This is from My plan and deceit against them. For this reason God the Almighty said: Indeed, My plan is firm, meaning great for whoever disobeys My command, belies My messengers, and dares to disobey Me. In the two Sahihs, it is narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: God, the Most High, gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape. Then he recited: “And such is the punishment of your Lord when He seizes towns while they are wrongdoers. Indeed, His punishment is painful and severe.” And the words of God, the Most High: Or do you ask them for a reward, so they are burdened with a heavy loss? Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write down? Its interpretation was presented in Surat At-Tur. The meaning of that is that you, O Muhammad, are calling them to God, the Mighty and Sublime, without taking a reward from them, rather you hope for a reward for that from God, the Most High, while they deny what you have brought them, merely out of ignorance, disbelief, and stubbornness.
68:47: When God Almighty mentioned that the righteous will have gardens of bliss with their Lord, He explained when that will happen and occur, saying: The Day the shin will be laid bare and they will be called to prostrate, but they will not be able, meaning the Day of Resurrection and the horrors, earthquakes, calamities, trials, and great matters that will occur on it. Al-Bukhari said here: Adam told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Yazid, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Our Lord will uncover His shin, and every believing man and woman will prostrate to Him. Whoever used to prostrate in this world for show and to be heard will remain, and he will go to prostrate, but his back will become flat.” This hadith is narrated in the two Sahihs and in other chains of transmission, and it has different wordings, and it is a long and well-known hadith. Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak said, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, The Day the shin will be uncovered, he said: It is the Day of Resurrection, a day of distress and hardship. Ibn Jarir narrated it, then he said: Ibn Hamid told us, Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Masoud or Ibn Abbas - the doubt is from Ibn Jarir - The Day the shin will be uncovered, he said: About a great matter, like the saying of the poet: The war has turned from its leg Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid, On the Day the shin is laid bare, meaning the severity of the matter. Ibn Abbas said, It is the first hour of the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Jarir said on the authority of Mujahid, On the Day the shin is laid bare, meaning the severity and seriousness of the matter. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, His statement, ‘On the Day the shin is laid bare,’ is the severe and terrible matter of terror on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, His statement, ‘On the Day the shin is laid bare,’ means when the matter is laid bare and deeds become apparent, and its laying bare means entering the Hereafter and the matter is laid bare from it. Ad-Dahhak and others narrated this on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir narrated all of this, then he said, Abu Zayd `Umar ibn Shabah told me, Harun ibn `Umar Al-Makhzumi told us, Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, Abu Sa`id Ruh ibn Janah told us, on the authority of a client of `Umar ibn `Abd Al-`Aziz, on the authority of Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, On the Day the shin is laid bare, meaning a great light before which they prostrate themselves. Abu Ya`la narrated it on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, on the authority of Al-Walid ibn Muslim, with it, and in it is a man. It is unclear, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: Their eyes will be humbled, humiliation will cover them meaning in the Hereafter because of their crimes and arrogance in this world, so they were punished with the opposite of what they were doing. And when they were called to prostrate in this world and refused to do so despite their good health and safety, likewise they will be punished with their inability to do so in the Hereafter. When the Lord Almighty appears, the believers will prostrate to Him, and none of the disbelievers or hypocrites will be able to prostrate. Rather, their backs will return to being level, and whenever one of them wants to prostrate, he will fall on his back, the opposite of prostration, as they were in this world, unlike what the believers are doing. Then God the Almighty said: So leave Me and him who denies this statement, meaning the Qur’an. This is a severe threat, meaning leave Me and him, for I know more about it than he does how to lure him and extend his error and give him respite, then I will seize him with the grasp of the Mighty, the Powerful. For this reason God the Almighty said: We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know, meaning while they are unaware, rather they believe that this is an honor from God, while in reality it is an insult, as God the Almighty said: Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children * We hasten to them with good things? Rather, they do not perceive. And God the Almighty said: “But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the gates of every [good] thing until, just as they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair.” For this reason He said here: “And grant them respite. Indeed, My plan is firm,” meaning I will delay them, give them respite, and grant them respite. This is from My plan and deceit against them. For this reason God the Almighty said: Indeed, My plan is firm, meaning great for whoever disobeys My command, belies My messengers, and dares to disobey Me. In the two Sahihs, it is narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: God, the Most High, gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape. Then he recited: “And such is the punishment of your Lord when He seizes towns while they are wrongdoers. Indeed, His punishment is painful and severe.” And the words of God, the Most High: Or do you ask them for a reward, so they are burdened with a heavy loss? Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write down? Its interpretation was presented in Surat At-Tur. The meaning of that is that you, O Muhammad, are calling them to God, the Mighty and Sublime, without taking a reward from them, rather you hope for a reward for that from God, the Most High, while they deny what you have brought them, merely out of ignorance, disbelief, and stubbornness.
68:49: God Almighty says: "So be patient" O Muhammad, with your people's harm to you and their denial, for God will judge you against them and make the outcome for you and your followers in this world and the hereafter. "And do not be like the companion of the fish" meaning Dhul-Nun, who is Jonah, son of Matta, peace be upon him, when he went angry with his people. What happened to him was that he rode into the sea and the fish swallowed him and the fish wandered with him in the seas and the darkness of the deep sea, and he heard the sea and what was in it glorifying the Most High, the Almighty, who does not reject what He has implemented of decree. Then he called out in the darkness, "There is no god except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers." God Almighty said: "So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers." God Almighty said: "And had he not been among those who glorify God, he would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected." And He said here: "When he called out while he was distressed." Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and As-Suddi said: And he was distressed. Ata' said: Al-Khurasani and Abu Malik: He was distressed. We have already mentioned in the hadith that when he said: “There is no god but You, glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers,” the word came out encircling the throne. The angels said: O Lord, this is a weak, well-known voice from a strange land. God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: Do you not know this? They said: No. He said: This is Yunus. They said: O Lord, Your servant, whose righteous deeds and answered supplications are continually being raised up to Him? He said: Yes. They said: Will You not have mercy on what he did in times of ease and save him from calamity? So God commanded the whale to throw him out onto the shore. For this reason, God, the Most High, said: So his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous. Imam Ahmad said: “Waki’ narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘It is not appropriate for anyone to say, “I am better than Jonah, son of Matta.”’ Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, and it is in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. God, the Most High, said: Those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others said: They would almost make you slip means they would pierce you with their eyes, meaning they would envy you with their eyes, because of their hatred for you, were it not for God’s protection and safeguarding you from them. This verse is evidence that the evil eye’s affliction and effect are real by the command of God, the Almighty, as has been reported in the hadiths narrated through many different chains of narration. Hadith of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him Abu Dawud said: Sulayman bin Dawud al-Atki told us, Sharik told us H and al-Abbas al-Anbari told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Sharik told us on the authority of al-Abbas bin Dharih on the authority of al-Sha’bi, al-Abbas said on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye, a fever, or blood that cannot be stopped. Al-Abbas did not mention the evil eye, and this is the wording of Sulayman. The hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husaib (may God be pleased with him Abu Abdullah ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr told us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Razi, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Buraydah ibn al-Husaib, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a fever. This is how Ibn Majah narrated it. Muslim included it in his Sahih on the authority of Sa`id ibn Mansur, on the authority of Hishayn ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of `Amir al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Buraydah, with a missing chain of transmission, and there is a story in it. Shu`bah narrated it on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Buraydah. This hadith was narrated by al-Bukhari on the authority of Muhammad ibn Fadil, Abu Dawud on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, and al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah, all three of them on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of `Amir al-Sha`bi, on the authority of `Imran ibn Husayn, with a missing chain of transmission: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a fever. Hadith of Abu Dharr Jundub bin Junada, may God be pleased with him Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Arara bin Al-Yazid Al-Sami told us, Daylam bin Ghazwan told us, Wahb bin Abi Dani told us, on the authority of Abu Harb, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The evil eye afflicts a man, by God’s permission, and he soars high, then falls from it. Its chain of transmission is strange, and they did not include it. Hadith of Habis At-Tamimi Imam Ahmad said: Abd Al-Samad told us, Harb told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us, Hayyah bin Habis At-Tamimi told me that his father told him that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: There is nothing wrong with a squint, and the evil eye is true, and the most truthful omen is an omen. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Ali, on the authority of Abu Ghassan Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ali bin Mubarak, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, with it, then he said: It is strange. And he said: Sinan narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Hayyah bin Habis, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I say: Imam Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Hasan bin Musa and Husayn bin Muhammad, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Hayyah, who told him on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There is nothing wrong with a squint, and the evil eye is true, and the most truthful omen is an omen. Hadith of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Duraid, Ismail bin Thauban told me, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The evil eye is real, the evil eye is real and brings down the witch. Strange. Another chain of transmission Muslim said in his Sahih: Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Darimi told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Wahib told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The evil eye is real, and if anything could overtake destiny, it would be the evil eye. And when you are asked to wash, then wash.” He is the only one who transmitted it, not Al-Bukhari. Abdul Razzaq said, on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Minhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, used to seek refuge for Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, saying: I seek refuge for you in the perfect words of God from every devil and pest, and from every evil eye. And he would say: This is how Ibrahim used to seek refuge for Isaac and Ishmael, peace be upon them. Al-Bukhari and the Sunan scholars transmitted it from the hadith of Al-Minhal with it. Hadith of Abu Umamah As`ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, may God be pleased with him Ibn Majah said: Hisham ibn `Ammar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Umamah As`ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: “`Amir ibn Rabi`ah passed by Sahl ibn Hunayf while he was bathing and said: I have never seen anything like today, nor such hideous skin. It was not long before he was struck by a snake, and he was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said to him: ‘He caught Sahl lying dead.’ He said: ‘Who do you accuse?’ They said: ‘`Amir ibn Rabi`ah.’ He said: ‘Why would one of you kill his brother? If one of you sees something he likes in his brother, let him pray for blessings for him.’ Then he called for water and ordered `Amir to perform ablution, washing his face and hands up to the elbows, his knees, and the inside of his lower garment, and he ordered him to pour water over himself.” Sufyan said: Mu`mar said, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, and he ordered that the vessel be tipped over from behind him. Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah and Malik ibn Anas, both of them from Al-Zuhri with it, and from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah also narrated it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Umamah: The vessel should be tipped over from behind. And from the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi’b on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Umamah: As’ad ibn Sahl ibn Hanif on the authority of his father on his authority. And from the hadith of Malik also on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl on the authority of his father on his authority. Hadith of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Sa`id bin Sulayman told us, `Ibad told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek protection from the eyes of the jinn and the eyes of mankind. When the two Mu`awwidhat were revealed, he took them and left everything else. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Sa`id bin Iyas Abu Mas`ud Al-Jariry, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan. Another hadith from him Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, my father told me, Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhaib told me, Abu Nadrah told me, on the authority of Abu Sa`id, “That Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Are you ill, O Muhammad? He said: Yes. He said: In the name of God I perform ruqyah over you from everything that is harming you, and from the evil of every soul and eye that is harming you, and God heals you. In the name of God I perform ruqyah over you.” And he narrated it on the authority of Affan on the authority of Abd al-Warith, similarly. Muslim and the people of Sunan, except Abu Dawud, narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Warith with it. Imam Ahmad also said: Affan told us, Wahib told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed or Jabir ibn Abdullah, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell ill, so Gabriel came to him and said, ‘In the name of God, I perform ruqyah over you from everything that is harming you, from every envier and evil eye, and God will heal you.’” It was also narrated by Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Tafawi, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on its authority. Abu Zur’ah al-Razi said: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Abu Nadra, and on the authority of Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Anas, with a similar meaning, and both are authentic. Hadith of Abu Hurairah (may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Ma'mar told us, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurairah told us, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: The evil eye is real. Both of them narrated it from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq. Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah, on the authority of al-Jariry, on the authority of Mudharib ibn Hazn, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The evil eye is real. He was the only one who narrated it. Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah, on the authority of Saeed al-Jariry, and Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numair told us, Thawr - meaning Ibn Yazid - told us, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The evil eye is real, and Satan and the envy of the sons of Adam attend to it. Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid told us, Abu Ma'shar told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays: Abu Hurairah was asked: Did you hear the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: “Superstition is in three things: in a dwelling, a horse, and a woman?” He said: I said, then, should I say about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something he did not say, but I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, The most truthful omen is the omen, and the evil eye is true. The hadith of Asma bint Umays Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Urwah ibn Amir, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Rifa’ah az-Zurqi, who said: “Asma said, ‘O Messenger of God, the children of Ja’far are afflicted by the evil eye. Should I recite ruqyah for them?’ He said, ‘Yes, for if anything could overtake destiny, it would be the evil eye.’” This is how it was narrated by at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah with this chain of transmission. It was also narrated by at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa’i from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Urwah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Urwah ibn Amir, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Rifa’ah, on the authority of Asma bint Umays with this chain of transmission. At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan saheeh. Hadith of Aisha (may God be pleased with her Ibn Majah said: Ali ibn Abi Al-Khasib told us, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan and Mis’ar, on the authority of Ma’bad ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded her to seek protection from the evil eye. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Kathir, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ma’bad ibn Khalid, and Muslim included it on the authority of Sufyan and Mis’ar, both on the authority of Ma’bad, on his authority. Then Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abu Hisham Al-Makhzumi told us, Wahib told us, on the authority of Abu Waqid, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Seek refuge in God, for the evil eye is real. He is the only one who narrated it. Abu Dawud said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The one who cast the evil eye would be ordered to perform ablution and wash the one who had been affected by it. I said likewise that Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Hasan bin Musa and Husayn bin Muhammad on the authority of Sinan that Ibn Hasana told him on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no inspiration, and the evil eye is real, and the most truthful omen is the omens. Hadith of Sahl ibn Hanif Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us. Abu Uwais told us. Al-Zuhri narrated to us on the authority of Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, that his father told him: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and they walked with him towards Mecca until they reached the ravine of Al-Kharrar in Al-Juhfah. Sahl ibn Hunayf washed himself. He was a white man with a handsome body and skin. Amir ibn Rabi’ah, the brother of Banu ‘Adi ibn Ka’b, looked at him while he was washing and said: ‘I have never seen anything like today, nor skin as hidden.’ Sahl became weak and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was approached and it was said to him: ‘O Messenger of God, what do you think of Sahl? By God, he does not raise his head nor does he recover.’ He said: ‘Do you accuse anyone of him?’ They said: ‘Amir ibn Rabi’ah looked at him.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Amir and became angry with him and said: ‘Why would one of you kill his brother? Why don’t you, when you see something that pleases you, bless him?’ Then he said: ‘Gaze for him.’ He washed his face, hands, elbows, knees, the tips of his feet, and the inside of his lower garment in a cup. Then he poured that water over him. A man poured it over his head and back from behind him, then he poured it over his head and back from behind him. The cup was behind him, so he did that and Sahl went with the people without any problem.” Hadith of Amir bin Rabi’ah Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: We were told by Wakee’, we were told by my father, we were told by Abdullah bin Isa, on the authority of Umayyah bin Hind bin Sahl bin Hunaif, on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Amir, who said: Amir bin Rabi’ah and Sahl bin Hunaif set out intending to perform ablution. He said: They set out looking for wine. He said: Amir put down the woolen cloak he was wearing, and I looked at him and caught his eye. He went down into the water to bathe. He said: I heard a crackling sound in the water, so I went to him and called out to him three times, but he did not answer me. So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He said: He came walking and waded into the water, and it was as if I could see the whiteness of his shins. He said: He struck his chest with his hand and then said: O God, turn away from him its heat and its cold and its rain. He said: He stood up, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you sees something he likes in his brother, in himself, or in his wealth, then let him ask for blessings, for the evil eye is real. Hadith of Jabir Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Muhammad bin Muammar narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Talib bin Habib bin Amr bin Sahl Al-Ansari, who is called Ibn Al-Dajji’, the companion of Hamza, may God be pleased with him, narrated to me Abdul Rahman bin Jabir bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘Most of those who die from my nation after the Book of God, His judgment and decree are because of the souls.’” Al-Bazzar said: He meant the evil eye. He said: We do not know of this hadith being narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, except with this chain of transmission. I said: Rather, it has been narrated from Jabir through another chain of transmission. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdul Rahman Muhammad bin Al-Mundhir Al-Harawi, known as Shukr, said in his book Al-Aja’ib, which contains important and strange benefits: Al-Ramadi narrated to us, Ya’qub bin Muhammad narrated to us, Ali bin Abi Ali Al-Hashemi narrated to us, Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir narrated to us, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘The evil eye is real, for it leads a man to the grave and a camel to the cooking pot. Most of the destruction of my nation is because of the evil eye.’” Then he narrated it on the authority of Shu`ayb ibn Ayoub, on the authority of Mu`awiyah ibn Hisham, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A man may enter the grave with an eye, and a camel may enter the cooking pot. This chain of transmission is all trustworthy, but it was not included in the Sahih. Hadith of Abdullah bin Amr Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah told us, Rashdin bin Saad told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Thauban, on the authority of Hisham bin Abi Ruqayyah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no contagion, no bad omen, no evil eye, no envy, and the evil eye is real. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Hadith on the authority of Ali Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Khaithama bin Sulaiman Al-Hafiz, who said: Ubaid bin Muhammad Al-Kashuri told us, Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Abd Rabbih Al-Basri told us on the authority of Abu Raja’ on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, “That Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and found him sad, so he said: O Muhammad, what is this sadness that I see on your face? He said: Al-Hasan and Al-Hussain have been afflicted by the evil eye. He said: He spoke the truth about the evil eye, for the evil eye is real, so why don’t you protect them with these words? He said: What are they, O Gabriel?” He said: Say: O God, Possessor of the mighty power and the ancient favor, Possessor of the noble face, Possessor of the perfect words and the answered supplications, save al-Hasan and al-Husayn from the souls of the jinn and the eyes of mankind. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said it, and they stood playing in front of him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Protect yourselves, your women, and your children with this incantation, for no one has ever sought protection with anything like it. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said: Abu Raja Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hanti from the people of Tustar was the only one who narrated it. Ibn Asakir mentioned him in the biography of Tarad ibn al-Husayn in his history. And the Almighty said: {And they say: He is mad} meaning they look down on him with their eyes and hurt him with their tongues and they say: He is mad, meaning because he came with the Qur’an. God the Almighty said: {And it is not but a reminder to the worlds} [the end of the interpretation of Surah Nun]. And to God be praise and thanks.
68:50: God Almighty says: So be patient O Muhammad, with your people's harm to you and their denial, for God will judge you against them and make the outcome for you and your followers in this world and the hereafter. And do not be like the companion of the fish meaning Dhul-Nun, who is Jonah, son of Matta, peace be upon him, when he went angry with his people. What happened to him was that he rode into the sea and the fish swallowed him and the fish wandered with him in the seas and the darkness of the deep sea, and he heard the sea and what was in it glorifying the Most High, the Almighty, who does not reject what He has implemented of decree. Then he called out in the darkness, "There is no god except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers." God Almighty said: "So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers." God Almighty said: And had he not been among those who glorify God, he would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected. And He said here: When he called out while he was distressed. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and As-Suddi said: And he was distressed. Ata' said: Al-Khurasani and Abu Malik: He was distressed. We have already mentioned in the hadith that when he said: “There is no god but You, glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers,” the word came out encircling the throne. The angels said: O Lord, this is a weak, well-known voice from a strange land. God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: Do you not know this? They said: No. He said: This is Yunus. They said: O Lord, Your servant, whose righteous deeds and answered supplications are continually being raised up to Him? He said: Yes. They said: Will You not have mercy on what he did in times of ease and save him from calamity? So God commanded the whale to throw him out onto the shore. For this reason, God, the Most High, said: So his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous. Imam Ahmad said: “Waki’ narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘It is not appropriate for anyone to say, “I am better than Jonah, son of Matta.”’ Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, and it is in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. God, the Most High, said: Those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others said: They would almost make you slip means they would pierce you with their eyes, meaning they would envy you with their eyes, because of their hatred for you, were it not for God’s protection and safeguarding you from them. This verse is evidence that the evil eye’s affliction and effect are real by the command of God, the Almighty, as has been reported in the hadiths narrated through many different chains of narration. Hadith of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him Abu Dawud said: Sulayman bin Dawud al-Atki told us, Sharik told us H and al-Abbas al-Anbari told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Sharik told us on the authority of al-Abbas bin Dharih on the authority of al-Sha’bi, al-Abbas said on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye, a fever, or blood that cannot be stopped. Al-Abbas did not mention the evil eye, and this is the wording of Sulayman. The hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husaib (may God be pleased with him Abu Abdullah ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr told us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Razi, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Buraydah ibn al-Husaib, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a fever. This is how Ibn Majah narrated it. Muslim included it in his Sahih on the authority of Sa`id ibn Mansur, on the authority of Hishayn ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of `Amir al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Buraydah, with a missing chain of transmission, and there is a story in it. Shu`bah narrated it on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Buraydah. This hadith was narrated by al-Bukhari on the authority of Muhammad ibn Fadil, Abu Dawud on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, and al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah, all three of them on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of `Amir al-Sha`bi, on the authority of `Imran ibn Husayn, with a missing chain of transmission: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a fever. Hadith of Abu Dharr Jundub bin Junada, may God be pleased with him Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Arara bin Al-Yazid Al-Sami told us, Daylam bin Ghazwan told us, Wahb bin Abi Dani told us, on the authority of Abu Harb, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The evil eye afflicts a man, by God’s permission, and he soars high, then falls from it. Its chain of transmission is strange, and they did not include it. Hadith of Habis At-Tamimi Imam Ahmad said: Abd Al-Samad told us, Harb told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us, Hayyah bin Habis At-Tamimi told me that his father told him that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: There is nothing wrong with a squint, and the evil eye is true, and the most truthful omen is an omen. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Ali, on the authority of Abu Ghassan Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ali bin Mubarak, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, with it, then he said: It is strange. And he said: Sinan narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Hayyah bin Habis, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I say: Imam Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Hasan bin Musa and Husayn bin Muhammad, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Hayyah, who told him on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There is nothing wrong with a squint, and the evil eye is true, and the most truthful omen is an omen. Hadith of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Duraid, Ismail bin Thauban told me, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The evil eye is real, the evil eye is real and brings down the witch. Strange. Another chain of transmission Muslim said in his Sahih: Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Darimi told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Wahib told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The evil eye is real, and if anything could overtake destiny, it would be the evil eye. And when you are asked to wash, then wash.” He is the only one who transmitted it, not Al-Bukhari. Abdul Razzaq said, on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Minhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, used to seek refuge for Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, saying: I seek refuge for you in the perfect words of God from every devil and pest, and from every evil eye. And he would say: This is how Ibrahim used to seek refuge for Isaac and Ishmael, peace be upon them. Al-Bukhari and the Sunan scholars transmitted it from the hadith of Al-Minhal with it. Hadith of Abu Umamah As`ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, may God be pleased with him Ibn Majah said: Hisham ibn `Ammar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Umamah As`ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: “`Amir ibn Rabi`ah passed by Sahl ibn Hunayf while he was bathing and said: I have never seen anything like today, nor such hideous skin. It was not long before he was struck by a snake, and he was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said to him: ‘He caught Sahl lying dead.’ He said: ‘Who do you accuse?’ They said: ‘`Amir ibn Rabi`ah.’ He said: ‘Why would one of you kill his brother? If one of you sees something he likes in his brother, let him pray for blessings for him.’ Then he called for water and ordered `Amir to perform ablution, washing his face and hands up to the elbows, his knees, and the inside of his lower garment, and he ordered him to pour water over himself.” Sufyan said: Mu`mar said, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, and he ordered that the vessel be tipped over from behind him. Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah and Malik ibn Anas, both of them from Al-Zuhri with it, and from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah also narrated it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Umamah: The vessel should be tipped over from behind. And from the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi’b on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Umamah: As’ad ibn Sahl ibn Hanif on the authority of his father on his authority. And from the hadith of Malik also on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl on the authority of his father on his authority. Hadith of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Sa`id bin Sulayman told us, `Ibad told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek protection from the eyes of the jinn and the eyes of mankind. When the two Mu`awwidhat were revealed, he took them and left everything else. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Sa`id bin Iyas Abu Mas`ud Al-Jariry, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan. Another hadith from him Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, my father told me, Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhaib told me, Abu Nadrah told me, on the authority of Abu Sa`id, “That Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Are you ill, O Muhammad? He said: Yes. He said: In the name of God I perform ruqyah over you from everything that is harming you, and from the evil of every soul and eye that is harming you, and God heals you. In the name of God I perform ruqyah over you.” And he narrated it on the authority of Affan on the authority of Abd al-Warith, similarly. Muslim and the people of Sunan, except Abu Dawud, narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Warith with it. Imam Ahmad also said: Affan told us, Wahib told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed or Jabir ibn Abdullah, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell ill, so Gabriel came to him and said, ‘In the name of God, I perform ruqyah over you from everything that is harming you, from every envier and evil eye, and God will heal you.’” It was also narrated by Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Tafawi, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on its authority. Abu Zur’ah al-Razi said: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Abu Nadra, and on the authority of Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Anas, with a similar meaning, and both are authentic. Hadith of Abu Hurairah (may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Ma'mar told us, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurairah told us, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: The evil eye is real. Both of them narrated it from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq. Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah, on the authority of al-Jariry, on the authority of Mudharib ibn Hazn, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The evil eye is real. He was the only one who narrated it. Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah, on the authority of Saeed al-Jariry, and Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numair told us, Thawr - meaning Ibn Yazid - told us, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The evil eye is real, and Satan and the envy of the sons of Adam attend to it. Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid told us, Abu Ma'shar told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays: Abu Hurairah was asked: Did you hear the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: “Superstition is in three things: in a dwelling, a horse, and a woman?” He said: I said, then, should I say about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something he did not say, but I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, The most truthful omen is the omen, and the evil eye is true. The hadith of Asma bint Umays Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Urwah ibn Amir, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Rifa’ah az-Zurqi, who said: “Asma said, ‘O Messenger of God, the children of Ja’far are afflicted by the evil eye. Should I recite ruqyah for them?’ He said, ‘Yes, for if anything could overtake destiny, it would be the evil eye.’” This is how it was narrated by at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah with this chain of transmission. It was also narrated by at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa’i from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Urwah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Urwah ibn Amir, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Rifa’ah, on the authority of Asma bint Umays with this chain of transmission. At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan saheeh. Hadith of Aisha (may God be pleased with her Ibn Majah said: Ali ibn Abi Al-Khasib told us, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan and Mis’ar, on the authority of Ma’bad ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded her to seek protection from the evil eye. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Kathir, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ma’bad ibn Khalid, and Muslim included it on the authority of Sufyan and Mis’ar, both on the authority of Ma’bad, on his authority. Then Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abu Hisham Al-Makhzumi told us, Wahib told us, on the authority of Abu Waqid, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Seek refuge in God, for the evil eye is real. He is the only one who narrated it. Abu Dawud said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The one who cast the evil eye would be ordered to perform ablution and wash the one who had been affected by it. I said likewise that Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Hasan bin Musa and Husayn bin Muhammad on the authority of Sinan that Ibn Hasana told him on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no inspiration, and the evil eye is real, and the most truthful omen is the omens. Hadith of Sahl ibn Hanif Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us. Abu Uwais told us. Al-Zuhri narrated to us on the authority of Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, that his father told him: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and they walked with him towards Mecca until they reached the ravine of Al-Kharrar in Al-Juhfah. Sahl ibn Hunayf washed himself. He was a white man with a handsome body and skin. Amir ibn Rabi’ah, the brother of Banu ‘Adi ibn Ka’b, looked at him while he was washing and said: ‘I have never seen anything like today, nor skin as hidden.’ Sahl became weak and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was approached and it was said to him: ‘O Messenger of God, what do you think of Sahl? By God, he does not raise his head nor does he recover.’ He said: ‘Do you accuse anyone of him?’ They said: ‘Amir ibn Rabi’ah looked at him.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Amir and became angry with him and said: ‘Why would one of you kill his brother? Why don’t you, when you see something that pleases you, bless him?’ Then he said: ‘Gaze for him.’ He washed his face, hands, elbows, knees, the tips of his feet, and the inside of his lower garment in a cup. Then he poured that water over him. A man poured it over his head and back from behind him, then he poured it over his head and back from behind him. The cup was behind him, so he did that and Sahl went with the people without any problem.” Hadith of Amir bin Rabi’ah Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: We were told by Wakee’, we were told by my father, we were told by Abdullah bin Isa, on the authority of Umayyah bin Hind bin Sahl bin Hunaif, on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Amir, who said: Amir bin Rabi’ah and Sahl bin Hunaif set out intending to perform ablution. He said: They set out looking for wine. He said: Amir put down the woolen cloak he was wearing, and I looked at him and caught his eye. He went down into the water to bathe. He said: I heard a crackling sound in the water, so I went to him and called out to him three times, but he did not answer me. So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He said: He came walking and waded into the water, and it was as if I could see the whiteness of his shins. He said: He struck his chest with his hand and then said: O God, turn away from him its heat and its cold and its rain. He said: He stood up, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you sees something he likes in his brother, in himself, or in his wealth, then let him ask for blessings, for the evil eye is real. Hadith of Jabir Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Muhammad bin Muammar narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Talib bin Habib bin Amr bin Sahl Al-Ansari, who is called Ibn Al-Dajji’, the companion of Hamza, may God be pleased with him, narrated to me Abdul Rahman bin Jabir bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘Most of those who die from my nation after the Book of God, His judgment and decree are because of the souls.’” Al-Bazzar said: He meant the evil eye. He said: We do not know of this hadith being narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, except with this chain of transmission. I said: Rather, it has been narrated from Jabir through another chain of transmission. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdul Rahman Muhammad bin Al-Mundhir Al-Harawi, known as Shukr, said in his book Al-Aja’ib, which contains important and strange benefits: Al-Ramadi narrated to us, Ya’qub bin Muhammad narrated to us, Ali bin Abi Ali Al-Hashemi narrated to us, Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir narrated to us, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘The evil eye is real, for it leads a man to the grave and a camel to the cooking pot. Most of the destruction of my nation is because of the evil eye.’” Then he narrated it on the authority of Shu`ayb ibn Ayoub, on the authority of Mu`awiyah ibn Hisham, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A man may enter the grave with an eye, and a camel may enter the cooking pot. This chain of transmission is all trustworthy, but it was not included in the Sahih. Hadith of Abdullah bin Amr Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah told us, Rashdin bin Saad told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Thauban, on the authority of Hisham bin Abi Ruqayyah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no contagion, no bad omen, no evil eye, no envy, and the evil eye is real. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Hadith on the authority of Ali Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Khaithama bin Sulaiman Al-Hafiz, who said: Ubaid bin Muhammad Al-Kashuri told us, Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Abd Rabbih Al-Basri told us on the authority of Abu Raja’ on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, “That Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and found him sad, so he said: O Muhammad, what is this sadness that I see on your face? He said: Al-Hasan and Al-Hussain have been afflicted by the evil eye. He said: He spoke the truth about the evil eye, for the evil eye is real, so why don’t you protect them with these words? He said: What are they, O Gabriel?” He said: Say: O God, Possessor of the mighty power and the ancient favor, Possessor of the noble face, Possessor of the perfect words and the answered supplications, save al-Hasan and al-Husayn from the souls of the jinn and the eyes of mankind. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said it, and they stood playing in front of him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Protect yourselves, your women, and your children with this incantation, for no one has ever sought protection with anything like it. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said: Abu Raja Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hanti from the people of Tustar was the only one who narrated it. Ibn Asakir mentioned him in the biography of Tarad ibn al-Husayn in his history. And the Almighty said: {And they say: He is mad} meaning they look down on him with their eyes and hurt him with their tongues and they say: He is mad, meaning because he came with the Qur’an. God the Almighty said: {And it is not but a reminder to the worlds} [the end of the interpretation of Surah Nun]. And to God be praise and thanks.
68:51: God Almighty says: "So be patient" O Muhammad, with your people's harm to you and their denial, for God will judge you against them and make the outcome for you and your followers in this world and the hereafter. "And do not be like the companion of the fish" meaning Dhul-Nun, who is Jonah, son of Matta, peace be upon him, when he went angry with his people. What happened to him was that he rode into the sea and the fish swallowed him and the fish wandered with him in the seas and the darkness of the deep sea, and he heard the sea and what was in it glorifying the Most High, the Almighty, who does not reject what He has implemented of decree. Then he called out in the darkness, "There is no god except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers." God Almighty said: "So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers." God Almighty said: "And had he not been among those who glorify God, he would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected." And He said here: "When he called out while he was distressed." Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and As-Suddi said: And he was distressed. Ata' said: Al-Khurasani and Abu Malik: He was distressed. We have already mentioned in the hadith that when he said: “There is no god but You, glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers,” the word came out encircling the throne. The angels said: O Lord, this is a weak, well-known voice from a strange land. God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: Do you not know this? They said: No. He said: This is Yunus. They said: O Lord, Your servant, whose righteous deeds and answered supplications are continually being raised up to Him? He said: Yes. They said: Will You not have mercy on what he did in times of ease and save him from calamity? So God commanded the whale to throw him out onto the shore. For this reason, God, the Most High, said: So his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous. Imam Ahmad said: “Waki’ narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘It is not appropriate for anyone to say, “I am better than Jonah, son of Matta.”’ Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, and it is in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. God, the Most High, said: Those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others said: They would almost make you slip means they would pierce you with their eyes, meaning they would envy you with their eyes, because of their hatred for you, were it not for God’s protection and safeguarding you from them. This verse is evidence that the evil eye’s affliction and effect are real by the command of God, the Almighty, as has been reported in the hadiths narrated through many different chains of narration. Hadith of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him Abu Dawud said: Sulayman bin Dawud al-Atki told us, Sharik told us H and al-Abbas al-Anbari told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Sharik told us on the authority of al-Abbas bin Dharih on the authority of al-Sha’bi, al-Abbas said on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye, a fever, or blood that cannot be stopped. Al-Abbas did not mention the evil eye, and this is the wording of Sulayman. The hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husaib (may God be pleased with him Abu Abdullah ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr told us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Razi, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Buraydah ibn al-Husaib, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a fever. This is how Ibn Majah narrated it. Muslim included it in his Sahih on the authority of Sa`id ibn Mansur, on the authority of Hishayn ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of `Amir al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Buraydah, with a missing chain of transmission, and there is a story in it. Shu`bah narrated it on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Buraydah. This hadith was narrated by al-Bukhari on the authority of Muhammad ibn Fadil, Abu Dawud on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, and al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah, all three of them on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of `Amir al-Sha`bi, on the authority of `Imran ibn Husayn, with a missing chain of transmission: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a fever. Hadith of Abu Dharr Jundub bin Junada, may God be pleased with him Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Arara bin Al-Yazid Al-Sami told us, Daylam bin Ghazwan told us, Wahb bin Abi Dani told us, on the authority of Abu Harb, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The evil eye afflicts a man, by God’s permission, and he soars high, then falls from it. Its chain of transmission is strange, and they did not include it. Hadith of Habis At-Tamimi Imam Ahmad said: Abd Al-Samad told us, Harb told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us, Hayyah bin Habis At-Tamimi told me that his father told him that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: There is nothing wrong with a squint, and the evil eye is true, and the most truthful omen is an omen. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Ali, on the authority of Abu Ghassan Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ali bin Mubarak, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, with it, then he said: It is strange. And he said: Sinan narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Hayyah bin Habis, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I say: Imam Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Hasan bin Musa and Husayn bin Muhammad, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Hayyah, who told him on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There is nothing wrong with a squint, and the evil eye is true, and the most truthful omen is an omen. Hadith of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Duraid, Ismail bin Thauban told me, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The evil eye is real, the evil eye is real and brings down the witch. Strange. Another chain of transmission Muslim said in his Sahih: Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Darimi told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Wahib told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The evil eye is real, and if anything could overtake destiny, it would be the evil eye. And when you are asked to wash, then wash.” He is the only one who transmitted it, not Al-Bukhari. Abdul Razzaq said, on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Minhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, used to seek refuge for Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, saying: I seek refuge for you in the perfect words of God from every devil and pest, and from every evil eye. And he would say: This is how Ibrahim used to seek refuge for Isaac and Ishmael, peace be upon them. Al-Bukhari and the Sunan scholars transmitted it from the hadith of Al-Minhal with it. Hadith of Abu Umamah As`ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, may God be pleased with him Ibn Majah said: Hisham ibn `Ammar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Umamah As`ad ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: “`Amir ibn Rabi`ah passed by Sahl ibn Hunayf while he was bathing and said: I have never seen anything like today, nor such hideous skin. It was not long before he was struck by a snake, and he was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said to him: ‘He caught Sahl lying dead.’ He said: ‘Who do you accuse?’ They said: ‘`Amir ibn Rabi`ah.’ He said: ‘Why would one of you kill his brother? If one of you sees something he likes in his brother, let him pray for blessings for him.’ Then he called for water and ordered `Amir to perform ablution, washing his face and hands up to the elbows, his knees, and the inside of his lower garment, and he ordered him to pour water over himself.” Sufyan said: Mu`mar said, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, and he ordered that the vessel be tipped over from behind him. Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah and Malik ibn Anas, both of them from Al-Zuhri with it, and from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah also narrated it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Umamah: The vessel should be tipped over from behind. And from the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi’b on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Umamah: As’ad ibn Sahl ibn Hanif on the authority of his father on his authority. And from the hadith of Malik also on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl on the authority of his father on his authority. Hadith of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Sa`id bin Sulayman told us, `Ibad told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek protection from the eyes of the jinn and the eyes of mankind. When the two Mu`awwidhat were revealed, he took them and left everything else. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Sa`id bin Iyas Abu Mas`ud Al-Jariry, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan. Another hadith from him Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, my father told me, Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhaib told me, Abu Nadrah told me, on the authority of Abu Sa`id, “That Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Are you ill, O Muhammad? He said: Yes. He said: In the name of God I perform ruqyah over you from everything that is harming you, and from the evil of every soul and eye that is harming you, and God heals you. In the name of God I perform ruqyah over you.” And he narrated it on the authority of Affan on the authority of Abd al-Warith, similarly. Muslim and the people of Sunan, except Abu Dawud, narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Warith with it. Imam Ahmad also said: Affan told us, Wahib told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed or Jabir ibn Abdullah, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell ill, so Gabriel came to him and said, ‘In the name of God, I perform ruqyah over you from everything that is harming you, from every envier and evil eye, and God will heal you.’” It was also narrated by Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Tafawi, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on its authority. Abu Zur’ah al-Razi said: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Abu Nadra, and on the authority of Abd al-Aziz, on the authority of Anas, with a similar meaning, and both are authentic. Hadith of Abu Hurairah (may God be pleased with him Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Ma'mar told us, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurairah told us, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: The evil eye is real. Both of them narrated it from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq. Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah, on the authority of al-Jariry, on the authority of Mudharib ibn Hazn, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The evil eye is real. He was the only one who narrated it. Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah, on the authority of Saeed al-Jariry, and Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numair told us, Thawr - meaning Ibn Yazid - told us, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: The evil eye is real, and Satan and the envy of the sons of Adam attend to it. Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid told us, Abu Ma'shar told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays: Abu Hurairah was asked: Did you hear the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) say: “Superstition is in three things: in a dwelling, a horse, and a woman?” He said: I said, then, should I say about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something he did not say, but I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, The most truthful omen is the omen, and the evil eye is true. The hadith of Asma bint Umays Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Urwah ibn Amir, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Rifa’ah az-Zurqi, who said: “Asma said, ‘O Messenger of God, the children of Ja’far are afflicted by the evil eye. Should I recite ruqyah for them?’ He said, ‘Yes, for if anything could overtake destiny, it would be the evil eye.’” This is how it was narrated by at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah with this chain of transmission. It was also narrated by at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa’i from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Urwah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Urwah ibn Amir, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Rifa’ah, on the authority of Asma bint Umays with this chain of transmission. At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan saheeh. Hadith of Aisha (may God be pleased with her Ibn Majah said: Ali ibn Abi Al-Khasib told us, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan and Mis’ar, on the authority of Ma’bad ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded her to seek protection from the evil eye. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Kathir, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ma’bad ibn Khalid, and Muslim included it on the authority of Sufyan and Mis’ar, both on the authority of Ma’bad, on his authority. Then Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abu Hisham Al-Makhzumi told us, Wahib told us, on the authority of Abu Waqid, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Seek refuge in God, for the evil eye is real. He is the only one who narrated it. Abu Dawud said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The one who cast the evil eye would be ordered to perform ablution and wash the one who had been affected by it. I said likewise that Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Hasan bin Musa and Husayn bin Muhammad on the authority of Sinan that Ibn Hasana told him on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no inspiration, and the evil eye is real, and the most truthful omen is the omens. Hadith of Sahl ibn Hanif Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us. Abu Uwais told us. Al-Zuhri narrated to us on the authority of Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, that his father told him: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and they walked with him towards Mecca until they reached the ravine of Al-Kharrar in Al-Juhfah. Sahl ibn Hunayf washed himself. He was a white man with a handsome body and skin. Amir ibn Rabi’ah, the brother of Banu ‘Adi ibn Ka’b, looked at him while he was washing and said: ‘I have never seen anything like today, nor skin as hidden.’ Sahl became weak and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was approached and it was said to him: ‘O Messenger of God, what do you think of Sahl? By God, he does not raise his head nor does he recover.’ He said: ‘Do you accuse anyone of him?’ They said: ‘Amir ibn Rabi’ah looked at him.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Amir and became angry with him and said: ‘Why would one of you kill his brother? Why don’t you, when you see something that pleases you, bless him?’ Then he said: ‘Gaze for him.’ He washed his face, hands, elbows, knees, the tips of his feet, and the inside of his lower garment in a cup. Then he poured that water over him. A man poured it over his head and back from behind him, then he poured it over his head and back from behind him. The cup was behind him, so he did that and Sahl went with the people without any problem.” Hadith of Amir bin Rabi’ah Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: We were told by Wakee’, we were told by my father, we were told by Abdullah bin Isa, on the authority of Umayyah bin Hind bin Sahl bin Hunaif, on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Amir, who said: Amir bin Rabi’ah and Sahl bin Hunaif set out intending to perform ablution. He said: They set out looking for wine. He said: Amir put down the woolen cloak he was wearing, and I looked at him and caught his eye. He went down into the water to bathe. He said: I heard a crackling sound in the water, so I went to him and called out to him three times, but he did not answer me. So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He said: He came walking and waded into the water, and it was as if I could see the whiteness of his shins. He said: He struck his chest with his hand and then said: O God, turn away from him its heat and its cold and its rain. He said: He stood up, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you sees something he likes in his brother, in himself, or in his wealth, then let him ask for blessings, for the evil eye is real. Hadith of Jabir Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Muhammad bin Muammar narrated to us, Abu Dawud narrated to us, Talib bin Habib bin Amr bin Sahl Al-Ansari, who is called Ibn Al-Dajji’, the companion of Hamza, may God be pleased with him, narrated to me Abdul Rahman bin Jabir bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘Most of those who die from my nation after the Book of God, His judgment and decree are because of the souls.’” Al-Bazzar said: He meant the evil eye. He said: We do not know of this hadith being narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, except with this chain of transmission. I said: Rather, it has been narrated from Jabir through another chain of transmission. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdul Rahman Muhammad bin Al-Mundhir Al-Harawi, known as Shukr, said in his book Al-Aja’ib, which contains important and strange benefits: Al-Ramadi narrated to us, Ya’qub bin Muhammad narrated to us, Ali bin Abi Ali Al-Hashemi narrated to us, Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir narrated to us, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘The evil eye is real, for it leads a man to the grave and a camel to the cooking pot. Most of the destruction of my nation is because of the evil eye.’” Then he narrated it on the authority of Shu`ayb ibn Ayoub, on the authority of Mu`awiyah ibn Hisham, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A man may enter the grave with an eye, and a camel may enter the cooking pot. This chain of transmission is all trustworthy, but it was not included in the Sahih. Hadith of Abdullah bin Amr Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah told us, Rashdin bin Saad told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Thauban, on the authority of Hisham bin Abi Ruqayyah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no contagion, no bad omen, no evil eye, no envy, and the evil eye is real. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Hadith on the authority of Ali Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated on the authority of Khaithama bin Sulaiman Al-Hafiz, who said: Ubaid bin Muhammad Al-Kashuri told us, Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Abd Rabbih Al-Basri told us on the authority of Abu Raja’ on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, “That Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and found him sad, so he said: O Muhammad, what is this sadness that I see on your face? He said: Al-Hasan and Al-Hussain have been afflicted by the evil eye. He said: He spoke the truth about the evil eye, for the evil eye is real, so why don’t you protect them with these words? He said: What are they, O Gabriel?” He said: Say: O God, Possessor of the mighty power and the ancient favor, Possessor of the noble face, Possessor of the perfect words and the answered supplications, save al-Hasan and al-Husayn from the souls of the jinn and the eyes of mankind. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said it, and they stood playing in front of him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Protect yourselves, your women, and your children with this incantation, for no one has ever sought protection with anything like it. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said: Abu Raja Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hanti from the people of Tustar was the only one who narrated it. Ibn Asakir mentioned him in the biography of Tarad ibn al-Husayn in his history. And the Almighty said: {And they say: He is mad} meaning they look down on him with their eyes and hurt him with their tongues and they say: He is mad, meaning because he came with the Qur’an. God the Almighty said: {And it is not but a reminder to the worlds} [the end of the interpretation of Surah Nun]. And to God be praise and thanks.

And do not be like the companion of the fish meaning Dhul-Nun, who is Jonah, son of Matta, peace be upon him, when he went angry with his people. What happened to him was that he rode into the sea and the fish swallowed him and the fish wandered with him in the seas and the darkness of the deep sea, and he heard the sea and what was in it glorifying the Most High, the Almighty, who does not reject what He has implemented of decree. Then he called out in the darkness, "There is no god except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers." God Almighty said: "So We responded to him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers." God Almighty said: And had he not been among those who glorify God, he would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected. And He said here: When he called out while he was distressed. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and As-Suddi said: And he was distressed. Ata' said: Al-Khurasani and Abu Malik: He was distressed. We have already mentioned in the hadith that when he said: “There is no god but You, glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers,” the word came out encircling the throne.
